## REQ-017 — Phase 2 NW-08 + NW-09 + NW-12 One pricing rewrite: Competitive / Market / Premium, ZIP-aware, labor + materials
**Source:** new-working-issues.md NW-08, NW-09 (PDF p7), NW-12 (PDF p21), 2026-09-18
**Requirement (client's words):** "The price tiers cannot be 'Basic / Standard / Premium' with descriptions like 'Basic paint job with minimal prep'… Use: Competitive — price-conscious bid when the job is straightforward and winning the work is the priority. Market — typical professional price for this type of work in your area. Premium — appropriate for urgent scheduling, difficult access, higher service expectations, or other job complexity." · "When calculating the price, are you using the Dragon's zip code?" · "For PM I don't know whether that includes materials. That is a vital question." — the three tiers are Competitive / Market / Premium with fixed localized labels, the model prices for the contractor's saved city/state/ZIP, prices include labor and materials and the screen says so.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/i18n-dictionary-consistency.test.ts` ("REQ-017 …") · integration (Deno) `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/suggest-prices/int.test.ts` + jest `jest/integration/suggest-prices.int.test.ts` · e2e `cypress/e2e/quotes-help-me-price.cy.ts` ("REQ-017 …")
**Model decision (Step 10):** the pricing call carries a per-request `model` override (new `LLMRequest.model`, honoured by `OpenAILLMClient`) and asks for `gpt-4o`; `SUGGEST_PRICES_MODEL` overrides it. Every other call keeps `OPENAI_MODEL` (default gpt-4o-mini). Live probe, client's 2,000 sq ft repaint with an Austin 78701 address: gpt-4o-mini $3,000 / $4,000 / $5,000 and $4,000 / $5,000 / $6,000; gpt-4o $5,500 / $6,500 / $7,500 and $6,500 / $8,000 / $9,500 (client's Claude/ChatGPT comparison: $6.5k–$16k).

## REQ-026 — 5.1 NW-05 Honest scope bullets from raw text — the fallbacks never echo the contractor's sentence
**Source:** new-working-issues.md NW-05 (PDF p4), 2026-09-18
**Requirement (client's words):** "The AI must never echo the user's raw input back as the suggested description. (Screenshot: all three 'I Need To' options just repeat 'I need to replace a toile for $500'.) We are the ones professionalizing the quotes." — when the model cannot be used (call failed, unparseable reply, dev stub) both fallbacks derive honest scope bullets (intent opener, price clause and pricing question stripped; one bullet per line) instead of bulleting the raw sentence, title the job from that scope (never "I Need To"), and report `degraded: true`; a usable model reply passes through with `degraded: false`.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/scope-from-raw.test.ts` ("REQ-026 …", pure helper `shared/quote-flow/scope-from-raw.ts`) · integration (Deno) `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/generate-job-options/int.test.ts` + `polish-job-details/int.test.ts` ("REQ-026 …") · e2e `n/a — the live dev server runs the real model; the fallback path is only reachable under the stub, which the Deno tests drive directly`
**Repro (before):** stub LLM → options `[{"jobName":"I Need To","bullets":["I need to replace a toile for $500"]}, …]`, polish `description: "I need to replace a toile for $500"`. **After:** `[{"jobName":"Replace A Toile","bullets":["Replace a toile"]}, …]`, polish `description: "Replace a toile", degraded: true`.
**Note:** `jest/integration/ux-job-name.int.test.ts` fails 4 cases against this dev server before and after (it pins the stub fallback's titles, but the dev server runs the real model: "Pintura Sala Comedor", "Reemplazo de Tablas") — pre-existing, unchanged by this work.

## REQ-027 — 5.2 NW-11 The job-details picker waits for the model; the heuristic is an honest error path
**Source:** new-working-issues.md NW-11 (PDF p20), 2026-09-18
**Requirement (client's words):** "Confirm the 'Confirm your job details' page is working correctly. (Screenshot: the three options are the raw text verbatim; 'Wider scope' only adds 'Jobsite cleanup'.)" — the picker shows "Writing up your options…" until the model answers instead of painting a client-side echo first; when the request fails or the server reports `degraded`, the cards are honest scope bullets (shared `scopeBulletsFromRaw`, never the typed sentence), a visible note says the draft could not be made, and the picker's "Write it myself" tile is prefilled with the contractor's own text.
**Decision:** the honest cards stay selected by default and the prefilled "Write it myself" tile opens on tap (the plan's "editor open" reading would make the raw sentence the default submission, which is exactly NW-05's complaint); the tile auto-opens only when nothing scope-like survived the contractor's text.
**Tests:** unit `n/a — the pure helper is pinned by REQ-026's jest/unit/scope-from-raw.test.ts` · integration `n/a — front-end only` · e2e `cypress/e2e/ux-help-me-price.cy.ts` ("REQ-027 …": delayed response → dots before any card; 500 → note + honest bullets + prefilled tile)

## REQ-028 — 5.3 NW-05 The prompts stop licensing the echo
**Source:** new-working-issues.md NW-05 (PDF p4), 2026-09-18
**Requirement (client's words):** "The AI must never echo the user's raw input back as the suggested description. … We are the ones professionalizing the quotes." — the job-options prompt states the rule ("Never return the contractor's sentence verbatim as a bullet or summary. Rewrite every bullet as a scope line; drop prices, 'I need to', and questions.") and the polish prompt's "mirror it back cleaned-up" clause is replaced by "write one neutral scope sentence from the facts given — never the contractor's own sentence"; both prompts stay English and identical in both dictionaries.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/i18n-dictionary-consistency.test.ts` ("REQ-028 …") · integration `n/a — prompt text; the model's behaviour is checked by a live probe recorded below` · e2e `n/a`
**Live probe (gpt-4o-mini, dev server, "I need to replace a toile for $500"):** before JSON mode the options call fell to the (honest) fallback 4 of 5 times — the model's reply was syntactically broken JSON (a missing brace between the es/en byLang blocks, captured by the new `[generate-job-options] reply not usable` warning). With `responseFormat: "json"` (OpenAI JSON mode, no chat tools on the one-shot calls) 6 of 6 probes returned three rewritten options ("Reemplazo de Inodoro" / "Instalación de Inodoro" / "Cambio de Inodoro", bullets like "Retirar inodoro existente", "Instalar inodoro nuevo", "Conectar fontanería"); polish → "Toilet Replacement", degraded:false.
**Tests (addendum):** integration (Deno) `generate-job-options/int.test.ts` + `polish-job-details/int.test.ts` ("REQ-026 … (b)"/"… passes through": the stub sees `responseFormat === "json"`) · `backend/src/agents/domain/data/openai/smk.test.ts` unchanged and green.

**Contracts:** `/api/auth/verify` (front-end proxy) answers **409** `{ ok:false, error:"account_closed", recoverable:true, recoveryToken }` for a closed account (loud for scripted logins); the backend `/auth/verify` answers 200 `{ ok:true, recoverable:true, recoveryToken }`; `POST /auth/recover` / `POST /auth/start-fresh` take `{ token }` and open the session. Danet registers every controller prototype method as a route, so controller helpers stay module functions.

## REQ-042 — Merge gate: the repo declares its suite in `.worktree-check`
**Source:** `/worktree-merge` triage on branch `new-working-issues`, 2026-09-19
**Requirement:** the merge gate must run the repo's real suites. With no `.worktree-check`, `worktree-merge` auto-detects `deno test -A` at the git root, which type-checks `jest/**/*.test.ts` (a Node/Jest harness outside the Deno workspace) and aborts on 2,340 `TS2304: Cannot find name 'expect'` errors before a single test runs — `develop` is red the same way — and would run the backend's KV tests without `--unstable-kv`. The executable `.worktree-check` at the git root now runs, in order: `cd backend && deno task test`, `cd front-end && deno check`, `cd jest && npm run test:unit`. Jest integration and Cypress stay out (they need the live dev server) and are reported through `--tested`.
**Tests:** `no tests — the gate script is itself the check; its first run is the merge's gate run recorded for this commit.`

Two conventions make the lane hold under the gate's own server: the lane drives `BASE_URL` as `localhost` (wt-gate names 127.0.0.1; the `/assistant?dev` seed button renders on localhost only), and the backend's KV file is derived from the served port (`scripts/gate-kv-path.ts`) so the specs' per-phone wipe (`dev-wipe-user.ts`, via `KV_PATH`) scrubs the store the gate is running on. The stub LLM drafts no quote from free text, so every assistant story under the gate starts from the dev seed (`seedPhase2`) — typing a job and getting a draft is only exercised by hand against the real client.

## REQ-050 — `/login-internal`: log in with an email address instead of a phone
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-01
**Requirement (client's words):** "i want to make a new login-internal route that will allow me to log in with email."
**Reading:** a hidden (unlinked) `/login-internal` page (`front-end/routes/login-internal.tsx`, island `LoginInternalForm`) takes an email address, the backend emails a 6-digit code to it, and `/verify-internal` (`front-end/routes/verify-internal.tsx`, the shared `CodeInput` in email mode) takes the code and opens the session — the same OTP discipline as the phone flow (5-minute code, 5 attempts, 30-second resend cooldown, dev master code `000000` off Deno Deploy). Email login is for EXISTING accounts only: the address must match the `email` on a user record (case-insensitive, trimmed); an unknown address answers a loud 404 `unknown_email` and never creates an account (the phone stays the identity). A closed account answers 409 `account_closed` (recovery is the phone flow's). No super-admin gate: any account with an email on file can use it.
**Contracts (backend, via the `/api` proxy):** `POST /auth/send-email-otp { email, language? }` → 200 `{ sent:true }` · 400 `invalid_email` · 404 `unknown_email` · 429 `cooldown` + Retry-After. `POST /auth/verify-email-otp { email, code }` → 200 `{ ok:true, sessionId, userId, isNewUser:false, redirectTo:"/dashboard?welcome=back" }` + `pm_session` cookie · 401 `invalid_code` · 410 `expired` · 429 `rate_limited` · 404 `unknown_email` · 409 `account_closed`. The OTP record is keyed `email:<address>` in the same store as the phone codes.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/normalize-email.test.ts` ("REQ-050 …", pure `shared/quote-flow/normalize-email.ts`) · integration (Deno) `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/send-email-otp/int.test.ts`, `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/verify-email-otp/int.test.ts` ("REQ-050 …") + `backend/src/users/entrypoints/auth-controller/e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-050 …") · e2e `e2e/login-internal/login-internal.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-050: …", the gate's story) + `cypress/e2e/auth-login-internal.cy.ts` ("REQ-050 …")

### REQ-050 AMENDMENT (2026-10-01) — an unknown email just creates the account
Raphael: "it needs to just create an account. rafac@monsterrg.com" — email login mirrors the phone flow: `POST /auth/send-email-otp` mails a code to ANY well-formed address (no more 404 `unknown_email`), and a correct code at `POST /auth/verify-email-otp` finds the account that carries the email or CREATES one (`isNewUser:true`, `redirectTo:"/welcome"`; the record carries the email, the OTP's language, the placeholder name, and an EMPTY phone — never a made-up one, because the user's phone is printed on documents and texted by the alerts). A closed account still answers 409 `account_closed`. Signing in with rafac@monsterrg.com on a fresh install creates that account.

## REQ-059 — A paid pick goes to the CRM's pay page in the same tab, and the receipt brings the person back with the plan active
**Source:** the same message: "v2 should redirect to the ui … the payments should be seamless between both apps … we should also use the nice card thing we made."
**Requirement (read from that):** picking a paid plan (onboarding or settings) sends THIS tab to the CRM's branded pay page (the flip pay card, REQ-013 there) — no popup, no second window. ## REQ-061 — Monthly billing: an active paid plan is charged to the card on file every month by the CRM; the plan shows the next bill, the card, and a month that did not go through
**Source:** the same message: "then we are able to do the card charging and the monthly billing, make sure all of this works 100%"
**Requirement (read from that):** the first month is paid on the CRM's pay page (REQ-059); the moment that settles, this app starts a monthly billing on the CRM (its REQ-081) for the plan's price, under the handle `pm:<userId>:<plan>`, the first recurring month a calendar month after activation, with the way back to settings for a recovery link. From then on the CRM's clock charges the card the person entered, with nobody pressing anything. The plan reads what the billing says: active shows "next bill <date>" and "Card on file: <brand> •••• <last4>"; a month the CRM could not collect makes the plan PAST DUE — the settings card says the payment didn't go through and "Pay now" opens that month's pay page, in this tab, and the receipt brings the person back current (nothing to check); a billing canceled on the CRM drops the plan to free. Going back to free cancels the billing (a CRM that will not take the cancel keeps the plan as it is); a switch of paid plan replaces the billing once the new plan's first month is paid. On the fakes the clock is `POST /me/plan/fake-bill` (404 against the real CRM), like fake-paid.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/business/plan/test.ts` ("REQ-061 plan — …", 4) · `backend/src/users/domain/data/payments-link/test.ts` ("REQ-061 payments-link fake — the clock …", "REQ-061 payments-link real — subscriptions go to the CRM's routes …") · `jest/unit/plan-return.test.ts` ("REQ-061 a past-due month goes to its pay page …") · int `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/choose-plan/int.test.ts` ("REQ-061 choose-plan — …", 3) · e2e `e2e/plan-picker/plan-picker.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-061: a month later the card on file is charged by itself and settings shows the next bill; with the card gone the month is past due — Pay now opens the page, and paying it makes the plan current again")

## REQ-072 — The login never waits on the CRM: the lead capture is fire and forget
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-14, on the prod login sitting on "…" for 22–31 s: "yeah fire and forget."
**Requirement (read from that):** `POST /auth/send-otp` answers `{sent:true}` the moment the code SMS is out; the REQ-060 lead capture (`CrmCustomerSync.capture` → the CRM's `POST /api/payments/customers`, which runs Quickbase calls that wait 10 s per 429) is started after the send and never awaited by the request — it still runs to completion and its failure is still only logged (capture already swallows and warns). Measured before: send-otp 22–31 s on prod while every KV-only call answered in 0.2 s and Twilio accepted the message within 1 s; the wait was the awaited capture.
**Stays:** the REQ-058 `crm.sync` after a NEW account's first verify is still awaited — not asked for here.
**Tests:** unit `n/a — the change is whether the controller awaits; nothing below the controller changes` · integration `backend/src/users/entrypoints/auth-controller/int.test.ts` ("REQ-072 send-otp answers before the CRM capture finishes, and the capture still reaches the CRM" — the in-process app against a stub CRM that holds the customers POST for 2.5 s: the reply comes back under a second, and the stub still receives the phone) · e2e `n/a — the stories run on the instant fake CRM; no page can show the wait`

### REQ-072 AMENDMENT (2026-10-14) — guaranteed, not merely un-awaited
Raphael, on the first cut (a bare un-awaited call): "what i mean by fire and forget is that is passes it to the backend and it does not block the user. it MUST be guaranteed to go in the crm this is mission critical." An un-awaited call is not a guarantee: on Deploy the isolate can die right after the reply (the app boots ~67 times an hour), and `capture` swallowed its failures. So the lead capture is an OUTBOX: `POST /auth/send-otp` writes `["crm-capture", phone]` to KV (ms) before it replies, and a sweep (`CrmLeadCapture.drain`) claims each due record, carries it to the CRM and deletes it only on the CRM's answer; a failure is deferred with backoff (5 s doubling, capped at 5 min — `lead-capture-retry`) and never dropped, loud in the log past 5 attempts. Sweeps run on every login, at boot (`backend/bootstrap/mod.ts`), and every minute on Deno Deploy's `Deno.cron` (`registerSweep`; the new Deploy runs Deno.cron and KV but NOT KV queues, per its migration guide — hence an outbox, not `kv.enqueue`). One sweep per process at a time; a 90 s lease keeps two processes off one record.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/business/lead-capture-retry/test.ts` ("REQ-072 backoff — …", "REQ-072 isDue — …") · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/int.test.ts` (5 "REQ-072 …" cases: record before send, failure deferred then landed, survives a restart, single-flight + lease, enqueue never waits) · `backend/src/users/entrypoints/auth-controller/int.test.ts` ("REQ-072 send-otp answers before the CRM capture finishes, and the capture still reaches the CRM") · e2e `n/a — the stories run on the instant fake CRM; no page can show the wait`
**Known:** the minute sweep needs `Deno.cron`, which Deno Deploy provides and a local `deno run` without `--unstable-cron` does not — there the login and boot sweeps carry the outbox; `registerSweep` reports which. The REQ-058 `crm.sync` on a NEW account's first verify stays awaited (not asked).

### REQ-071 AMENDMENT (2026-10-14) — one generated file stays
`front-end/ui-breakdown/viewer-data.js`, the one-line manifest `_viewer/gen.py` builds from the ui-breakdown markdown for the file:// viewer, keeps the old brand: regenerating it rewrites its single line, and the merge gate's clean step reads that line as new source and refuses the prose words "legacy" and "@deprecated" the specs contain (filed to claude-tools). The markdown it is built from is renamed; run `gen.py` once the gate exempts generated files.

### REQ-071 REVISION (2026-10-14) — the viewer manifest is renamed too, inline
The judge was right that the amendment above left a tracked file spelling the old brand. The manifest now lives INSIDE `front-end/ui-breakdown/viewer.html` (its `<script id="uib-data">` line, written by `_viewer/gen.py`, which rerenders the page in place); `viewer-data.js` is deleted. The viewer still works over file:// with no fetch, the renamed specs are what it shows, and the brand scan covers it like any tracked file.

The plan-picker stories "REQ-060: the phone typed into login is a CRM customer before any code is entered …" and "REQ-062: a person who never finishes …" pressed Enter on the phone box through the locator; the story runner stamps a frame after every locator press, and on Playwright 1.63 that screenshot hangs 90 s when the page is already navigating to /verify (the REQ-068 note; three gate runs in a row today; filed as coms claude-tools 20261014T223413Z-w11-64121). ## REQ-073 — The boot sweep and the cron registration never crash the isolate
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-15: "okay deploy it to prod." The first push of REQ-071/072 (main `917859f`, Deno Deploy revision `9b0565m49b6j`) built, booted, logged `Listening`, and then failed in the platform's warming step with `failure_reason: "error"` and no detail — twice, with no request served and nothing on stderr — while the same tree boots and stays up locally with and without `--unstable-cron`. The two lines REQ-072 added to boot are the only new code that runs before the first request, and both leave a promise nobody holds: `leads.registerSweep()` drops the promise `Deno.cron` returns, and `void leads.drain()` drops a sweep that rejects the moment KV cannot be opened or read. An un-held rejection ends a Deno process.
**Requirement (read from that):** nothing the lead-capture outbox does at boot can take the isolate down. `drain()` never rejects: a sweep that cannot read its outbox resolves `{ landed: 0, deferred: 0, waiting: 0, failed: <message> }` and logs it as an error (the records stay for the next sweep). `registerSweep(cron = Deno.cron)` holds the promise the registration returns and logs its rejection as a warning; a registration that throws, or no `Deno.cron` at all, is `false` and logged — either way the login and boot sweeps still carry the outbox. A KV open that fails is not remembered (`getKv` clears its cached promise on rejection) so the next sweep opens KV again. Boot logs one line saying whether the minute sweep is registered.
**Not proven:** the platform gives no detail for the failure; this removes the only two ways the new boot could end the process and makes the next failure name itself in the log.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/test.ts` ("REQ-073 drain — …", "REQ-073 registerSweep — …") + `backend/src/core/data/kv/test.ts` ("REQ-073 getKv — a failed open is not cached …") · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/int.test.ts` ("REQ-073 a sweep over a KV that will not open resolves with the failure logged, and the next sweep opens KV again") · e2e `n/a — a boot-time guard; the stories run on a healthy KV and no page shows it`

## REQ-074 — The minute sweep is a timer in the isolate, never Deno.cron
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-15: "okay deploy it to prod." Two pushes of main (`917859f` → revision `9b0565m49b6j`, `980fe04` → `gnmhf2ww8t07`) built, warmed up (`warmup: succeeded` in the revision's progress — the REQ-073 guard held; the boot line logged `minute sweep registered`) and then failed in the platform's **routing** step on every timeline (production, git-branch, preview) with `failure_reason: "error"` and no detail, leaving prod on the old revision. Three preview deployments of the same tree from the CLI isolated the cause: the tree as-is (the cron registered in `backend/bootstrap/mod.ts`) → routing errored (`kdkhgnawagsa`); the cron moved to the top level of `mod.ts`, as the Deploy docs ask → routing errored (`yk3r5fhqrnmt`); the same tree with no `Deno.cron` call at all → routed and serving (`4w88b4jzv6yt`, the DocuMonster login). The platform recorded `crons: false` for every one of them, so it never recognised the cron, and the Deploy docs say cron is unavailable on preview deployments while every revision of this app carries a preview timeline.
**Requirement (read from that):** no code path of the app calls `Deno.cron`. The REQ-072 minute sweep is `setInterval` inside the isolate (`CrmLeadCapture.registerSweep(timer = setInterval, unref = Deno.unrefTimer)`), unref'd so it never holds a process open: it sweeps every 60 s while an isolate lives, and the boot sweep and the login sweep carry the outbox as before. REQ-073 still holds for the timer: one that cannot be set is logged and never ends the process. Boot logs `minute sweep on a timer`.
**Retires:** REQ-073's `registerSweep(cron)` and its cron-rejection test (the cron path is gone, so is the test); the "every minute on Deno Deploy's cron" words of the REQ-072 amendment — a timer in the isolate now.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/test.ts` ("REQ-074 registerSweep — the minute sweep is an in-isolate timer: Deno.cron is never called", "REQ-074 registerSweep — the timer fires every 60 s and each tick sweeps the outbox; the timer never keeps the process alive and never throws") · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/int.test.ts` ("REQ-074 a boot sweep and a login sweep still carry the outbox with no cron anywhere") · e2e `n/a — a boot-time guard; no page shows it`

## REQ-077 — A server started for the gate or a pin runs on its own KV
**Source:** found by the judge on this branch, 2026-10-15 (`/wt:merge` for cron-sweep-to-timer): the gate's e2e lane went red on `e2e/login-internal` — a page this branch never touched — once in the gate (REQ-050, rafac@monsterrg.com) and, alone on the pin, twice more (REQ-063 hans@documonster.com; then REQ-050 login-internal.story@…), each "page.waitForURL: Timeout 90000ms" after the submit click, the frame showing the button still pending.
**Cause (proved):** `deno task serve` without a `KV_PATH` opens Deno's ONE default KV file for this checkout (`$DENO_DIR/location_data/<hash>/kv.sqlite3`, the same hash for the gate's server, the pinned server and every earlier run — its `-wal` carried both servers' writes). The login stories use fixed addresses by requirement, and a second code for the same address inside 30 s answers `429 {error:"cooldown"}` (P-03; shown by hand: two sends 1 s apart → 200 then 429). The island shows the cooldown and never navigates; the story waits out its 90 s. Reproduced deterministically: the stories twice back-to-back on one server → 4/4 then 3/4, the second run's send 11 s after the first's. By curl the endpoint answers in 10–30 ms every time, direct and through the proxy, under bursts too — the server was never slow.
**Requirement:** a server started on a bare `PORT` — what the merge gate (wt-gate, REQ-278) and `pin-link --serve` (REQ-287) hand the `serve` task — runs its backend on a fresh KV file in a temp dir of its own (`scripts/serve-kv.ts` `kvPathFor`; `serve.ts` passes it as `KV_PATH` to the backend child and prints `[serve] kv → <path>`). An explicit `KV_PATH` always wins. No `PORT` (a developer's own `deno task serve` on 5280/4280) keeps the platform default and its persistent dev data.
**Known:** a pinned server now starts empty on every `pin-link --serve`; the stories create what they show. Two runs against the SAME server inside 30 s still collide on a fixed address — that is the cooldown working, not the gate's case (one lane per fresh server).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/serve-kv.test.ts` ("REQ-077 a bare PORT with no KV_PATH gets a fresh KV file in its own temp dir"; "REQ-077 an explicit KV_PATH always wins, PORT or not"; "REQ-077 no PORT keeps the platform default — a developer's own serve keeps its data"; "REQ-077 two servers started one after the other never share a file") · integration `n/a — a process-launch rule; the live proof is below` · e2e `n/a — no page; the whole e2e lane is the consumer`
**Evidence (2026-10-15):** unit RED first (`Cannot find module '../../scripts/serve-kv'`), then 4/4 (jest unit 522 passed). Live: the pin restarted twice back-to-back, `[serve] kv → /tmp/v2-kv-8f698a4a6d87debc/kv.sqlite3` then `/tmp/v2-kv-18a8f7f1a18e3f40/kv.sqlite3`, and `e2e/login-internal` 4/4 on each, 20 s apart — the pairing that failed 3/4 on the shared file.

## REQ-080 — Facebook ads conversion tracking: a Meta Pixel on the ad funnel, behind META_PIXEL_ID
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-15: "i want to do facebook adverts here, need a tracking pixel to track conversions, what do i need to do?" then "okay can you build this in and how do i e2e test it so i can do it as a customer and make sure i see the result i expect in meta".
**Requirement:** the Meta Pixel loads on the ad funnel's pages only — the two websites ("/", "/landing"), the code page, the welcome wizard, the plan and pay pages, settings, login — never the dashboard, the assistant, the legal pages or a customer's document (`shared/meta-pixel/pixel.ts` isPixelPage). Which loader: Meta's (`connect.facebook.net`) on the real deploy with `META_PIXEL_ID` set; the app's own fake (`/meta-pixel-fake.js`, recording every call on `window.__pmPixel`) when `DENO_DEPLOY` is unset (REQ-318: the gate, a dev box, a pin); nothing on the real deploy without the id — ads tracking never takes the site down. Three conversions, each with a stable event id (a reload never counts twice — a localStorage key per id — and a server-side copy later deduplicates on Meta's side): **Lead** on the code page when it was reached by sending the code from a landing (`?px=lead`; the login page sends codes too and is not a lead), keyed by a hash of the phone; **CompleteRegistration** when a new account reaches /welcome, keyed by the account; **Subscribe** with the plan's price (value, USD, predicted_ltv = 12 months) when /plan/return finds the plan active and sends the person back with `?px=sub:<plan>:<due>` — to the wizard or to settings. The privacy policy's "Cookies and Analytics" section discloses the Meta Pixel, the `_fbp` cookie and what is shared, in English and in Spanish. `META_PIXEL_ID` is in `.env.example`.
**Known:** the policy's text changed but its date (`LEGAL_LAST_UPDATED`, the attorney's October 6, 2026) was left for Raphael to decide; the Conversions API (server-side events, for the iOS traffic the browser pixel loses) is not built — it needs a system-user token and would reuse these event ids. `front-end/islands/LandingScripts.tsx` builds a /verify url too but is not rendered by any route (comments only) and was left alone.
**How Raphael tests it as a customer (never an agent, REQ-318):** set `META_PIXEL_ID` on Deno Deploy (Events Manager → the dataset's id) and deploy. In Chrome with the Meta Pixel Helper extension: open paperworkmonster.com — the helper shows PageView with the id; enter a phone and send the code — on /verify the helper shows Lead; verify the code as a NEW number — on /welcome it shows CompleteRegistration; pick Monster and pay — back on /welcome it shows Subscribe with value 99. Events Manager → Data sources → the pixel → "Test events": the same four appear within a minute with the browser's test code (or in Overview a few minutes later). The repo's stories drive the same walk on the real services from the user's own headed `test:e2e:prod` run: they read the pixel's events from the fake's record on the gate and from the real loader's requests to `www.facebook.com/tr` on that run.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/meta-pixel.test.ts` (nine `REQ-080 …` cases: the loader rules, the page allowlist, the snippet, the three events and their ids, the once-per-browser script, the pages that carry it, `.env.example`, the privacy text in both languages, the stories' two readings) · integration n/a — no backend change; the pixel is SSR markup and a browser script, proven by the e2e lane · e2e `e2e/meta-pixel/meta-pixel.e2e.test.ts` (four stories: the pages that have it and the pages that do not; Lead once and not on a reload; CompleteRegistration once and not on a reload or a later visit; Subscribe from onboarding (99) and from settings (199), not on a reload).
**Evidence (2026-10-15):** RED first — unit: `Cannot find module '../../shared/meta-pixel/pixel'`; e2e: the Lead story's wait for `/verify?…&px=lead` timed out while the landing's success branch still sent `&lang=en` alone (the 429 branch had the marker, the success branch did not — a replace that matched one indentation). **Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-18, a screenshot of the /landing2 signup card in prod answering his own number with "No pudimos mandar el código. Inténtalo de nuevo.": "in prod, this makes no sesne" — then, on the diagnosis: "fix it."

## REQ-091 — Onboarding happens until every question is answered
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-18, after a team phone (540-333-1334) signed up at 12:29 PM ET while the site's API calls still went cross-origin to paperworkmonster.com — the session cookie landed on that host, the onboarding page found no session and bounced, and the evening's code landed on the dashboard as "welcome back": "well it did not show him the onboarding even though he is a new user. why?" — then: "onboarding must happen until we get answers to all the questions." Decided with him on the two open points: Skip stays and the wizard returns (not "no skipping at all"); the gate is every code verify and the dashboard (not sign-in only, not every app page).
**Requirement:** the wizard's nine questions — name, business name, email, plan, state, address, payment methods, logo, insurance — are each answered by the profile field the wizard saves it to, one rule for every page (`shared/quote-flow/onboarding-questions.ts`): the seeded placeholder is not a name, a paid pick still waiting on its pay page is not a plan, a payment-method map with nothing switched on is not an answer, blank is not an answer, and the skip stamp (`onboardedAt`, `POST /me/onboarded`) is a record of leaving the wizard, never a gate. Every verified code — phone, email, account recovery, start-fresh — lands in `/welcome` while any question is open and on `/dashboard?welcome=back` once none is: the backend decides (`redirectTo`, now on `/auth/verify-otp` too, `SignInLanding` reading the same profile snapshot) and the page follows — never the one-shot "new user" flag, which the bounced first sign-in had burned. `/dashboard` sends an account with an open question to `/welcome`, which resumes at the first open one; `/welcome` lets go to the dashboard only when nothing is open. Skip on a step puts that question off for now; "Skip setup for now" records the leave and drops the person in the assistant, since the dashboard would send them straight back. The logo and insurance questions no longer say "(optional)". The other app pages (the assistant, quotes, settings …) stay reachable, so the wizard's own side trips (the pay page, the sample quote) keep working. A profile the dashboard cannot read lets the person through rather than loop between two pages that cannot load.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/onboarding-questions.test.ts` ("REQ-091: …", 5 — the nine questions, the placeholder, each question's field, one open question lands in the wizard, no question is optional in the copy) · `backend/src/users/entrypoints/auth-controller/e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-091 auth e2e: verify-otp carries redirectTo — /welcome while any of the nine onboarding questions is open, /dashboard?welcome=back once all are answered"; the REQ-050 email case now expects `/welcome` for an account with eight questions open) · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/sign-in-landing/int.test.ts` ("REQ-091 sign-in-landing — …", 4: a fresh account and the skip stamp, all nine answered, each one open in turn, a pending plan) · e2e `e2e/onboarding-until-answered/onboarding-until-answered.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-091: onboarding happens until every question is answered — a new account's code lands in the wizard, Skip only puts a question off, 'Skip setup for now' leaves for the assistant, and the dashboard and the next code bring the wizard back at the first open question"; "REQ-091: with eight of nine answered the code still lands in the wizard at the open question; with all nine answered it lands on the dashboard, and /welcome lets go"). The stories that open the dashboard (legal-pages, assistant-shell, meta-pixel, login-internal) answer every question through `e2e/_shared/onboarding-answers.ts`; the cypress entry-point spec (on demand) now expects `/welcome` for the second code.
**Evidence (2026-10-18):** RED first — jest "Cannot find module '../../shared/quote-flow/onboarding-questions'", the int test failing type-check on the missing `sign-in-landing/mod.ts`, the story on "greeted as back" (the dashboard's toast drops `?welcome=back` from the address once it hydrates; the story reads the landing as sent). Then GREEN: jest 5/5; sign-in-landing 4/4; auth-controller e2e.test 14/14; `shots run` over onboarding-until-answered, legal-pages, assistant-shell, meta-pixel, login-internal, plan-picker and dev-code: 28 passed, 0 failed; lanes in the merge receipt. ## REQ-094 — The fine-tooth comb: what the audit of the shipped /landing2 found
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-19, on the REQ-092/093 worktree: "go through this with a fine tooth comb." The whole page audited against the v3 mock (`documonster-landing`) on the pin: the markup, the stylesheet (every rule matched against the page; the ones that match nothing are the demo's day picker, the code step, the thanks card and the motion states — none dead), both dictionaries side by side (111 keys, no gaps, no Spanish on the English page), every link's target (all 200, every `#` anchor exists), the images, the console (no errors), the network (no failed request but one), a desktop at 1280, a phone at 390 and a tablet at 820, in both languages.
**Requirement (what was found and is fixed here):** (1) the stylesheet's paragraph reset `.l2 p { margin: 0 }` (0,1,1) outranked every single-class margin on a `<p>`: the mock's `margin: -4px 0 4px` on the plan blurbs (`.l2-plan__sub`) and `margin-top: 6px` on the plans subtitle (`.l2-plans__sub`) never applied — the same cascade fact REQ-093 hit. The reset is now `.l2 :where(p)`, so a class's own margin wins and the mock's spacing applies; the Projects line keeps its 10px of padding (REQ-093), no margin. (2) On a tablet in portrait (761–860px, an iPad) the hero's 118%-wide monster image pushed the page wider than the screen — a sideways scroll (scrollWidth 839 at 820); the mock has the same CSS and the same overflow. `.l2-hero` now clips sideways (`overflow-x: clip`); the disc stays round. (3) The share image every landing's Open Graph and Twitter tags name — `/og-card.png`, declared 1200×630 in `shared/quote-flow/site-meta.ts` — was a 404 on prod and on the pin: the file was never tracked (no commit ever added it), so every share of "/", "/landing" or "/landing2" rendered without an image, the very thing those tags were written for. A 1200×630 card in the page's own style (the bunting, the wordmark, the Spanish headline, the monster on its disc, documonster.com) is now `front-end/static/og-card.png`. (4) The signup's phone field carried `required`, so an empty Empezar gratis got the browser's own tooltip in the browser's language instead of the page's `errPhone` message; the demo form had no such attribute. The attribute is gone: an empty send is answered on the page, in its language.
**Found and left as shipped (the mock's, flagged in the hand-off):** at 820px the 58px headline runs to five lines in a 369px column (the mock does the same); no `hreflang` alternate links for the two language variants of one URL (none of the three landings has them); the app shell's `theme-color` is the app's teal on a cream page; the footer's policy links are 20px-tall tap targets and the consent's Términos link 16px; the English hours say "EST" year-round; the English demo's email placeholder is `jose@tunegocio.com`.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/landing2-page.test.ts` ("REQ-094 the fine-tooth comb — what the audit of the shipped page found": the reset is `:where`-scoped and `.l2 p {` is gone, the two margins are declared; `.l2-hero` has `overflow-x: clip`; `front-end/static/og-card.png` is tracked, a PNG whose header says 1200×630, the size `OG_IMAGE` declares; the `#reg-phone` input has no `required` and the island answers with `errPhone`; and REQ-093's test now names the `:where` reset) · integration n/a — markup, stylesheet and a static file · e2e `e2e/landing2/landing2.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-094: the fine-tooth comb — on a tablet nothing is wider than the screen and the monster's disc stays round; the plan blurbs and the plans subtitle keep the mock's spacing; the share image every landing's og:image names answers at 1200×630; an empty Empezar gratis is answered on the page, in its language": at 820×1180 scrollWidth ≤ 820 and the disc's width equals its height; at 1280 the computed margins are -4px/4px and 6px and the Projects line's padding 10px; the og:image path fetched from the page answers 200 image/png and decodes to 1200×630; an empty Start free shows "Enter a valid cell number." and stays on the phone step).

## REQ-096 — The third comb over /landing2: the stylesheet is cache-busted, the English lines are marked and nothing else, the cards' titles are headings, the toggle says where it goes
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-19, after REQ-095's hand-off: "run the fine tooth comb again." The third pass went to the wire and the accessibility tree a second time: prod's cache headers for everything the page loads, `/landing2/` with a slash (200 on prod and the pin; the canonical names the bare path), `deno lint` and `deno fmt --check` on every landing2 file (clean), the phone formatter on letters and overlong input (`tenDigits` strips and caps), the lang marks REQ-095 added, the heading list, the toggle's accessible name, JSON-LD (none on any landing — left so). Found: (1) prod serves every static file without a build id as `no-cache, no-store` — the plain `<link href="/landing2.css">` was re-downloaded on every view — while a URL carrying `?__frsh_c=<build>` (every `<img>`, which Fresh rewrites itself) is `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; a plain link also means a changed stylesheet reaches everyone at once, so the fix must keep that. (2) REQ-095's `lang="en"` sat on the whole hero note, so its Spanish label "Tu cliente recibió" was read as English — my own slip, caught here; the team's "Monster Success Specialist" was unmarked. The other two landings link their stylesheets plainly too (`/landing.css`, `/promo.css`) — not touched here, named in the hand-off.
**Requirement:** (1) the stylesheet link is `href={asset("/landing2.css")}` (Fresh's `asset` from `fresh/runtime`): the URL carries the build id, so a browser keeps it until the build changes and never a stale one. ## REQ-098 — A new account's CRM customer is made after the sign-up replies, never before
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-20, on prod: "okay now in prod when i do a new sign up it takes forever after i enter the code. quicly tell me why" — "i think it has to do with the crm logic to capture the lead being synchronous, it should fire the event to the backend and forget about it while the backend finishes the request." — "just go to prod and look at the logs. dont guess."
**Found (prod, 2026-10-20 11:40–12:05 UTC):** every verify of a NEW account — `/auth/verify`, `/auth/verify-otp`, `/auth/verify-email-otp`, `/auth/start-fresh` — awaited `CrmCustomerSync.sync(userId)` before replying: four KV reads, then `POST /api/payments/customers` on the CRM app (`PPWK_PAYMENTS_URL` = ppwk-crm-dialer.thetechgoose.deno.net, a second Deno Deploy app) through a fetch with no timeout; the CRM's `customer.create` for a ref it has not seen opens a ledger account, saves to its KV and queries then inserts into Quickbase (api.quickbase.com, the service REQ-072 measured at 10 s per 429). Measured from the box: the CRM app answers a cold request in 5.2 s and a warm one in 0.2 s; documonster's own verify path answers in 0.18 s when the CRM is not involved. The app's logs (`deno deploy logs`, 136 217 records over four hours) show documonster booting a fresh isolate 75 times — nearly every visit is a cold start — and the CRM app booting one about every minute; no `[crm-customer-sync]` or `[crm-lead-capture]` warning in the window, so the sync was succeeding and the wait was the CRM finishing, not failing; the sign-up at 11:55:24 (GET /landing2) landed on /welcome at 11:56:01. Neither app logs API requests or durations, so the exact seconds of that verify are not in the logs; the chain above is what the reply waited for. `SIGNUP_NOTIFY_ENABLED` is unset in prod — the signup email is not in the chain.
**Requirement:** the account's CRM customer rides the lead outbox (REQ-072's pattern — "fire and forget … it MUST be guaranteed to go in the crm"): `CrmLeadCapture.enqueueSync(userId)` writes a KV record (`["crm-capture", "user", userId]`, a `PendingCapture` carrying `userId`) and starts the sweep without awaiting it; the four verify sites call that instead of the sync, so the reply comes back while the CRM still holds the customer; the sweep makes or revises the customer through `CrmCustomerSync.ensure`, clears the record on the CRM's answer, and a failure defers it with REQ-072's backoff — the boot, login and minute sweeps carry whatever an isolate left. A record enqueued while a sweep is on its list is swept right after that sweep, not left for the next login. `CrmCustomerSync` leaves the auth controller (REQ-281); the paid pick (`ChoosePlan`) and the profile edits keep their own synchronous `ensure`/`sync`, as before.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/test.ts` ("REQ-098 sweep — a record carrying a userId is the account's customer sync: carried by ensure and cleared by its record; a phone record stays a lead capture"; "REQ-098 a record enqueued while a sweep is running is swept right after it, not left for the next login") · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/int.test.ts` ("REQ-098 a customer sync is a KV record before anything is sent, enqueueSync never waits on the CRM, and the sweep makes the account's customer"; "REQ-098 a CRM that fails keeps the sync record with its attempts and error, and a later sweep makes the customer and clears it") and `backend/src/users/entrypoints/auth-controller/int.test.ts` ("REQ-098 verify-otp for a new account answers before the CRM has made its customer, and the customer still reaches the CRM": the stub CRM door holds the customer create; the verify replies within 3 s with the session and `redirectTo`; the customer reaches the door once with the account's phone; the record is pending in KV until the door answers, then cleared) · e2e n/a — the reply's timing is the backend's; on the fakes the CRM answers at once, and the page after the code is REQ-089's story.
**Evidence (2026-10-20):** RED first — the three files refused type-check on `enqueueSync` and `userId` (TS2339); with the sync awaited inside `enqueueSync` the controller test fails "the verify reply while the CRM holds the customer: not within 5000ms". Then GREEN: the three files 17 passed; `deno test src/users src/communication` 382 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (one run of three had `choose-plan/int.test.ts` REQ-064 fail with "POST /api/payments/customers: TypeError: fetch failed" from the REAL `CrmPaymentsLink` — a sibling file had flipped the process-wide `PPWK_PAYMENTS_*` env mid-run, the parallel-lane race the fixtures warn about; the file passes alone three times and the next full run was 382/0 — not this change's path); lanes in the gate at wt-show.

## REQ-099 — The wizard's saves reply before the CRM hears about them
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-20, on prod minutes after REQ-098 shipped: "now that otp shit works but every fucking onboarding question makes me wait. why the FUCK would you patch that and not this?"
**Found:** the same synchronous CRM customer sync REQ-098 took off the four verify sites was still on every write the wizard makes — `PUT /me` (the name step, the email step), `PUT /profile/identity` (the business name, the payment methods, the logo), `POST /me/onboarded` (leaving the wizard) and the free pick on `POST /me/plan` (plus the tier changes in `ChoosePlan.refresh`/`projected`): each awaited `CrmCustomerSync.sync` — the CRM app's cold start (5 s measured), its ledger account and its Quickbase query and insert, through a fetch with no timeout — before replying. Seven of the nine questions hit it. REQ-098's requirement said the profile edits "keep their own synchronous sync, as before"; that was the wrong scope for the symptom.
**Requirement:** every one of those writes enqueues the account's sync on the lead outbox (`CrmLeadCapture.enqueueSync`, REQ-098) and replies at once; the sweep carries the profile as last saved after the reply. Only the paid pick still waits on the CRM, because its pay link needs the customerId (`ensure`). A save made while the account's sync is already in flight is not lost: `addSync` re-marks the existing record (a new `enqueuedAt`, due now, the lease kept), the running sweep's `done` leaves a re-marked record with its lease cleared instead of deleting it, and the sweep that follows (REQ-098's `again`) carries the newer profile — so rapid successive answers coalesce into one CRM write carrying the latest state, never a stale one. `CrmCustomerSync.sync` (best effort, swallowing) has no caller left and is gone (REQ-281); `ensure` is the one door, throwing `payments-unavailable` for the sweep to defer. The `GET /me/crm-customer` read is unchanged.
**Tests:** unit n/a — the change is the controllers' call order and a KV compare-and-swap; the sweep's pure branches are REQ-098's unit tests · integration `backend/src/users/entrypoints/me-controller/int.test.ts` (new: "REQ-099 the wizard's saves — PUT /me, PUT /profile/identity, POST /me/plan free, POST /me/onboarded — reply before the CRM has taken the customer, and the CRM ends up with the profile as last saved": the stub CRM door holds every ref'd customer write; a new account's five saves each reply 200 within 3 s while it is held; one write is on the CRM and the saves did not line up behind it; the record is pending in KV; released, the record clears and the CRM's last write is "Ana Roofing" / contact "Ana" / tier Lead) · `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/int.test.ts` ("REQ-099 a save made while the account's sync is in flight is not lost: the record is re-marked, the sweep runs again after the first, and the CRM ends up with the newer profile") · `choose-plan/int.test.ts` (the coordinator takes the outbox; the tier assertions read after `leads.drain()`; `crm.sync` → `ensure`) · `crm-customer-sync/int.test.ts` (`sync` → `ensure`; the CRM-down case is `ensure` rejecting with payments-unavailable) · `load-profile` and `sign-in-landing` int tests build `ChoosePlan` with the outbox · e2e n/a — the reply's timing is the backend's; on the fakes the CRM answers at once, and the wizard's pages are REQ-091's stories (the drive runs them on the pin).
**Evidence (2026-10-20):** RED first — the four files refused type-check (`ChoosePlan` took four arguments); the two that compile failed at runtime: the controller test "the name: the reply while the CRM holds the customer: not within 5000ms", the outbox test with the second write missing. Then GREEN: the four files 33 passed; `deno test src/users src/communication` 384 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored; lanes in the gate at wt-show.

## REQ-100 — One source of truth for the merchant account: the pick names it, the pay link carries it, the footer prints it, the billing reads it; no env var has a say
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-20, with the JJS Global report open: "12670394611 POSTED. I CHECKED THE BOTTOM IT SAYS 'PRIMARY' AND THE CUSTOMER GOT NO RECEIPT AND … THERE IS NO PAYMENT IN THERE IT CHARGED IT ON THE TEST ACCOUNT EVEN THOUGH IT SAID PRIMARY"; "THE FOOTER'S PRIMARY LABEL SHOULD BE WHAT ACCOUNT WE ARE USING"; "THERE NEEDS TO BE A SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH WHEN IT REGARDS TO WHAT ACCOUNT IS BEING USED"; "THE FOOTER SHOWS WHAT MERCHANT ACCOUNT IS BEING USED. ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH SO IT CANNOT BE MIXED UP."
**Found:** NMI 12670394611 (2026-10-12 14:46Z, $99, visa 2139, CRM Finance charge 2652) went through the CRM account `sandbox` because this app's Deploy env had `PPWK_PAYMENTS_ACCOUNT=sandbox` from 2026-10-10 02:49Z to 2026-10-14 16:40Z (REQ-069's "the account every charge goes through"), while nothing a person could see said so: the pick's own merchant was `""` on every real plan, the real client filled the header from the env var, and a plan stored without a merchant started its billing on that same var. Three places could name the account — the env var, the pick's query param, the CRM's own record — and the page could print one while the charge went through another.
**Requirement (read from that):** the account a charge goes through is decided ONCE, by the one rule in `shared/quote-flow/merchant-accounts.ts` (`accountForPick`: the name the pick gives, else `sandbox` for the $1 test tier, `primary` for every real plan), at the pick (`ChoosePlan.choose`), and that one name is what the real client puts in the CRM's `x-account` header on the mint and on the billing, what the pay link's url carries (`account=`, the way the CRM's link does, ppwk-crm REQ-091), what the pay page's footer prints, and what the plan's record stores (`merchant`, required on every paid pick). The real client refuses a mint or a billing that names no account (`merchant-required`, 400) before any request — nothing defaults it; `PPWK_PAYMENTS_ACCOUNT` is not read any more and is deleted from Deploy (`.wt/prod.md`); the real client needs the CRM's url and token only, and a production boot names those two when either is missing. A plan stored before the account was recorded on it resolves by the same rule when its billing starts. The fake link builder mirrors the CRM: its page url carries `account=`, this app's stand-in pay page (`/pay/fake`) prints that account in its footer (`data-cy="fake-pay-account"`, `data-account`) and refuses a link that names none, so the stories prove the footer matches the account on every pick.
**Amends:** REQ-069 — `PPWK_PAYMENTS_ACCOUNT` is retired (see its AMENDMENT below); REQ-064 — "no merchant named = the CRM's default account" is retired (see its AMENDMENT below).
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/data/payments-link/test.ts` ("REQ-100 payments-link real — every mint and every subscription carries the pick's account in `x-account`; nothing named is refused by name, never defaulted; the CRM's 422 reads merchant-unknown", "REQ-064/100 payments-link fake — the link's url carries `account=<the pick's account>` …") · `backend/src/users/domain/business/payments-link-select/test.ts` ("REQ-054/100 …" ×3, "REQ-100 selectPaymentsLinkName: PPWK_PAYMENTS_ACCOUNT is not read") · `backend/src/users/domain/business/plan/test.ts` ("REQ-064/100 plan — a paid pick's record carries the account it was made with, always") · `jest/unit/merchant-accounts.test.ts` ("REQ-100 a plan pick that names nothing goes through primary") · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/choose-plan/int.test.ts` ("REQ-100 choose-plan — a plan pick naming nothing goes through primary: the pay link, the plan's record and the monthly billing all say primary, whatever PPWK_PAYMENTS_ACCOUNT says") · e2e `e2e/plan-picker/plan-picker.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-100: a paid pick from onboarding lands on a pay page whose footer reads the one account the charge goes through — primary — the same name the pay link and the plan's record carry")
**Prod step (REQ-374, `.wt/prod.md`):** `env delete PPWK_PAYMENTS_ACCOUNT` on paperwork-monsters-v2. The CRM half — its own pay page footer bound to the link's recorded account and the sale sent through that same record — is the CRM repo's (ppwk-crm REQ-101 prints the name; this app now always names one).

## REQ-101 — The merchant accounts: `primary` is the real one, `sandbox` the fake one, and more can be added on the CRM
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-20: "PRIMARY IS THE ACUTAL ACCOUNT AND SANDBOX IS THE FAKE ACCOUNT BUT WE CAN ADD MORE."; "you dont have to verify it just tell me where to put it in and i will define the accounts."
**Requirement (read from that):** the accounts are defined in ONE place, the CRM's Accounts tab (`/ui/payments/admin?tab=accounts`, ppwk-crm REQ-091: a name, the platform, the gateway key); this app names them and never holds a key. `primary` is the real account (real card, real money, settles at the gateway) and every real plan pick goes through it; `sandbox` is the fake account (test cards, nothing settles) and the hidden $1 test tier (`/plan/test`) goes through it unless its address names another (`?merchant=primary` charges primary; any slug the CRM has on record works the same way, so more can be added without a code change). `/plan/test` says, by name, which account its charge will go through, and the card's form carries that name. A name the CRM has no account on record for is refused by name — the CRM's 422 reads `merchant-unknown` here, nothing is minted, the plan stays as it was, and the page the pick came from says "That merchant account is not on record. Add it on the CRM's Accounts tab first" (`?plan=merchant-unknown`). The fake keeps the same record (`primary`, `sandbox`, plus whatever a test adds with `world.accounts.add`) and refuses the rest the same way. No gateway check is built: the name is trusted as defined there, as told.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/merchant-accounts.test.ts` ("REQ-101 primary is the real account and sandbox the fake one", "REQ-101 the $1 test tier goes through sandbox unless its address names another account", "REQ-101 a name on the pick wins for any plan") · `jest/unit/plan-return.test.ts` ("REQ-101 the CRM's 422 comes back as ?plan=merchant-unknown, and the page reads it") · `backend/src/users/domain/data/payments-link/test.ts` ("REQ-101 payments-link fake — primary and sandbox are on record; a name that is not is merchant-unknown (422) and nothing is minted; an account added to the record is admitted") · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/choose-plan/int.test.ts` ("REQ-101 choose-plan — the $1 test tier goes through sandbox unless the pick names another account; primary named is primary; a name the CRM has no record of is refused and nothing is stored", and the two REQ-064 tests, which now put `alpha` on record first) · e2e `e2e/plan-picker/plan-picker.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-101: /plan/test charges sandbox unless its address names another account; ?merchant=primary charges primary; a name not on record is refused and nothing is charged"; the REQ-064 story now picks sandbox)

### REQ-069 AMENDMENT (2026-10-20) — the third key is retired
`PPWK_PAYMENTS_ACCOUNT` is gone (REQ-100): the real client sends the pick's own account in `x-account`, never a configured default, and refuses a charge that names none. The real client selects on `PPWK_PAYMENTS_URL` + `PPWK_PAYMENTS_TOKEN` alone; a production boot throws naming whichever of the two is missing. The header rule itself stands.

### REQ-064 AMENDMENT (2026-10-20) — the test tier's account is sandbox, never "the CRM's default"
"No merchant named = the CRM's default account" is retired (REQ-100/101): the $1 test tier goes through `sandbox` unless `/plan/test?merchant=<name>` names another, the page says which, and a pick's record always carries its account. The pay link's url carries it as `account=` (the CRM's word), no longer `merchant=`.

## REQ-104 — A Monster Free signup gets the initial information and never meets the credit card ask
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-20: "Monster Free signup must get initial information and then skip credit card ask."
**Found:** every button into the /landing2 signup card — the nav's and the Monster Free card's "Empezar gratis", the final CTA's, the sticky bar's, and the two paid cards' "Registrarme" — led to the same card ("Empieza gratis en 30 segundos"), the same code and the same wizard, whose fourth question, right after the email, is "Pick your plan": the three cards, with the pay page (the card form) behind the two paid ones. A person who came to start free was asked for a plan, and shown the card ask, in the middle of the free signup. Free itself was already stored without a card (REQ-054); the ask was the step.
**Requirement (read from that):** a signup through the card is a Monster Free signup unless a paid card's Registrarme brought the person to it: every Empezar gratis button into the card names `free` (`data-plan`), each plan card's button names its plan, and the card shows the plan it signs up for (`data-plan` on `#empezar`: free when the page opens, the last button pressed after). The code posts the plan named (`POST /auth/verify-otp { plan }`; `/auth/verify` the same); for `free` the backend stores Monster Free on the account the moment it has no plan on record (`ChoosePlan.startFree`: a pick already made — pending, active, past due or free — stands untouched and no billing is touched; the CRM hears the tier by the outbox, REQ-099). The wizard asks its plan question only while the plan is not Monster Free (`front-end/lib/welcome-steps.ts`, the plan step's `asked`): a Monster Free account's wizard is nine steps — the name, the business, the email, then straight to the state, the address, the payment methods, the logo, the insurance and the sample quote — and never shows the cards or the pay page; after a pick it resumes at the step after the plan's slot whether the plan step is shown or not (REQ-059's `?after=plan`). A paid plan named with the code stores nothing: the wizard asks, as before, where the email and the pay page are (REQ-054/059). A plain code — /login, the other two landings — stores nothing either. The upgrade is where REQ-054 put it: the settings panel's cards. ## REQ-103 — Every sign-up generates an email to hello@documonster.com, after the reply
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-10-20: "if somone signs up we need to generate an email to hello@documonster.com"
**Found:** a signup alert existed in `VerifyOtp` (`notifyNewSignup`) but was OFF — `SIGNUP_NOTIFY_ENABLED` unset in prod (REQ-098's finding) — aimed at two personal addresses (`hp@hans.work`, `raphael@rcincorporated.net`, overridable by `SIGNUP_NOTIFY_EMAILS`), fired only on the phone flow (not the email login's new account, REQ-050, nor start-fresh, REQ-039), and was awaited inside the verify's reply: the Postmark call in the very chain REQ-098 cut the CRM out of. **Found in the gate, at the first hand-off:** the backend's `dev` task loads `../.env`, which from a worktree resolves to the primary checkout's `.env` (its `POSTMARK_API_KEY`, `TWILIO_*`, `DEV_LOG_OTP`), so the gate's `serve` runs with the REAL Postmark and Twilio keys: the two e2e runs mailed hello@documonster.com 70 times (Postmark's outbound log, 11:14–11:16 EDT, one per story sign-up, from warnings@monsterrg.com), and each real send held the sweep about 1.2 s, so the CRM syncs queued behind them landed late and the REQ-058/062 plan-picker stories read the unnamed dragon after the name was saved. The hole predates this change: the same log shows 62 real mails to the team inbox today from the stories' demo bookings, calls and contact forms, and 8 OTP mails to the blackhole address — every gate run mails the team.
**Requirement:** a sign-up — a NEW account opened by `/auth/verify`, `/auth/verify-otp`, `/auth/verify-email-otp` or `/auth/start-fresh` (`isNewUser`) — generates an email to `hello@documonster.com`: subject "New DocuMonster signup — <phone or email>", the body saying how they signed up (by phone / by email), the phone, the email, the language, the user id and the time the account was opened. The address is the one constant `SIGNUP_INBOX` (`backend/src/users/domain/business/signup-notice`, pure); no env var has a say. It rides the lead outbox, never the reply (REQ-072/098's "fire and forget … guaranteed"): `CrmLeadCapture.enqueueSignupNotice(userId)` writes a KV record (`["crm-capture", "signup-notice", userId]`, a `PendingCapture` with `kind: "signup-notice"`) before the reply and starts the sweep without awaiting it; the sweep (boot, login, minute) carries it through `SignupNotice.send` — the account as it is then, mailed through Postmark (`EmailService`; an account wiped before the sweep reached it is nothing to tell, the record clears) — clears it on Postmark's ok and defers a refusal with REQ-072's backoff, never dropping it. A sign-in to an existing account sends nothing. The flag, the two addresses and `notifyNewSignup` are deleted (REQ-281). On the fakes (REQ-318: `DENO_DEPLOY` unset and not on Deno Deploy — `onRealDeploy`, the one predicate in `backend/src/core/business/real-deploy`, now shared with REQ-082's dev code) the sweep logs `[signup-notice] fakes: would mail hello@documonster.com — <subject>` and counts the record as sent; Postmark is reached on the real deploy only.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/business/signup-notice/test.ts` ("REQ-103 signupNoticeEmail — every sign-up is an email to hello@documonster.com, and no env var has a say"; "… a phone sign-up: the subject names the phone, the body says how, the phone, the language, the id and the time, and never the placeholder name"; "… an email sign-up (no phone, REQ-050): the subject names the address, the body says email and prints no empty phone") · unit `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/test.ts` ("REQ-103 sweep — a signup-notice record is carried by SignupNotice.send and cleared by its record; a send Postmark refused is deferred with the reason, never dropped; the lead and the sync stay theirs") · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/crm-lead-capture/int.test.ts` ("REQ-103 a signup notice is a KV record before anything is sent, and enqueueSignupNotice never waits on the mail"; "REQ-103 the sweep mails hello@documonster.com with the account on it and clears the record; a mail Postmark refused keeps the record with its attempts and reason, and a later sweep mails it; an account wiped before its sweep is cleared with no mail") and `backend/src/users/entrypoints/auth-controller/int.test.ts` ("REQ-103 a sign-up — by phone on /auth/verify-otp and /auth/verify, by email, by start-fresh — answers at once, and the email to hello@documonster.com goes out after the reply with the account on it; a sign-in to an existing account sends none"; the REQ-098 test and `me-controller/int.test.ts` REQ-099 now read the sync record apart from the notice) · e2e n/a — no page changes: the email leaves the backend after the reply, on the fakes no mail leaves the box, and the sign-up pages are REQ-081/089/050's stories. Added at the first hand-off: unit `backend/src/core/business/real-deploy/test.ts` ("REQ-103 onRealDeploy — the fakes: neither switch set, or set blank"; "… the real deploy: DENO_DEPLOY set, or DENO_DEPLOYMENT_ID set") · unit `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/signup-notice/test.ts` ("REQ-103 SignupNotice — on the fakes (neither switch set) the notice is logged with its subject, Postmark is never reached, and the record counts as sent"; "… on the real deploy … the account's email goes to hello@documonster.com through Postmark; a refusal is thrown for the sweep to retry"; "… an account wiped before its sweep is nothing to tell: no mail, no throw, on either side of the switch") · integration `crm-lead-capture/int.test.ts` ("REQ-103 on the fakes (REQ-318: DENO_DEPLOY unset, not on Deno Deploy) the sweep logs the notice with its subject and clears it — Postmark is never reached"; its other REQ-103 tests and the controller's stand on the real side through the carrier's `env` seam).
