## REQ-137 — Field tasks live on the account's customers and bill through its invoices; neither customers nor invoices change
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-03: "in this demo we built clients and invoices. i dont want to redo clients and invoices; i dont want to redo that feature or change it at all but i needed it in the demo so that it would work. when i integrate it into the app i dont want to change those two things." / "okay build it out!"
**Context:** the A2Z demo (`programming/a2z`, built Oct 27–28 2026 on a copy of this app's shell) proved subscriptions → zones → a worker's day → a batch pull of completed work into draft invoices. Its own clients and invoices were stand-ins so it could run alone.
**Requirement (read from that):** the demo's new features come into this app as ONE new backend module, `field` (`backend/src/field/`), and new pages; the module reads customers through `CustomerStore` and writes invoices through `InvoiceStore` exactly as they are — no field is added to a customer or an invoice, no route of theirs changes, and the demo's own client and invoice screens, routes and store slices are not ported. A subscription names a customer by `customerId`; a task carries the id of the invoice it was billed on (that is the module's own record, not the invoice's). The existing /customers and /invoices pages are untouched.
**Tests:** unit n/a — a structural constraint · integration `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-137 the pull writes a real invoice: GET /invoices (the existing controller) lists it, draft, for the customer, with one line per task; the customer record is unchanged") · e2e n/a — covered by REQ-143's story reading the result on the existing /invoices page.
**Evidence (2026-11-03):** structural — `git diff develop --stat -- backend/src/crm backend/src/paperwork front-end/islands/ClientsPage.tsx front-end/islands/InvoicesPage.tsx` is empty: no customer or invoice file changed. The module reads `CustomerStore.getOwned` (subscriptions) and `CustomerStore.listByUser` (names) and writes `InvoiceStore.create` / `.update` (the pull, the send) — nothing else of theirs. ## REQ-138 — Workers: the owner creates each worker's login; a worker signs in with their cell and a 4-digit PIN; a foreman sees every crew

## REQ-139 — Subscriptions: a customer's recurring maintenance at an address, with task types and a price each, on a real schedule; the address is geocoded once
**Source:** the demo's REQ-018/019/021/022/035/044, kept as decided there.

## REQ-140 — Assignments: subscriptions group into zones by distance; one worker covers a zone; a dragged-in subscription stays where the owner put it
**Source:** the demo's REQ-020/022/023/036/041, kept as decided there.
**Requirement:** zones (`GET /field/regions`, each with its `worker` and active `subscriptions`) are computed in the backend from stored coordinates: every active subscription joins the nearest zone within 3 km or starts a new one (first unused letter name "Zona A…", first unused colour); existing zones keep id, name, colour and worker; a zone left empty with no worker is dropped; a zone's centre is its un-pinned members' centroid. `PUT /field/regions/:id/worker { workerId | null }` staffs it, and today's and later open tasks of that zone move to that worker. `POST /field/subscriptions/:id/move { regionId }` pins the subscription to that zone through every re-grouping (a paused one is refused 409; its own zone is a no-op); `POST /field/subscriptions/:id/unpin` lets it group by distance again; `POST /field/regions/regroup` re-runs the grouping.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/regions/test.ts` ("REQ-140 groupRegions — near/far, pure, join-or-start keeping ids and workers, pinned stays, empty-unstaffed dropped, a far pin never ejects members, unique names and colours") · integration `field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-140 zones — staffing a zone; a move sticks across a regroup; unpin releases it; open tasks follow the zone's new worker") · e2e the story staffs a zone on /field/assignments.

## REQ-141 — The day's tasks: generated from the staffed zones' due subscriptions; the office notes and prices; the worker checks off, adds, removes, defers and notes — never seeing a price
**Source:** the demo's REQ-007..011/025..029/032/035/037/039/043, kept as decided there.
**Requirement:** `GET /field/tasks?date=` lists the account's tasks for a day with customer, type, worker and zone names (today's round is generated on first read — idempotent: one task per subscription × item × date, only for subscriptions due that day in a staffed zone, the address and price snapshotted); `POST /field/tasks/generate { date }` does the same for any day and reports the due subscriptions with no worker (never dropped silently); `PATCH /field/tasks/:id { adminNote?, priceCents? }` is the office's note and price (a price on an invoiced task is 409). Worker side (pm_worker cookie): `GET /field/worker/tasks?date=&all=1` — only their own tasks (every worker's for a foreman asking `all=1`, theirs first), with no price, no invoice id, no office note, and `locked` once invoiced; `POST /field/worker/tasks/:id/complete { note? }`, `/uncomplete`, `/skip` (not done — never invoiced), `/restore`, `/defer { note? }` (tomorrow's copy holds the slot, the original marked), `/note { note }` (the visit's note, on every task of that visit); `POST /field/worker/visits/:subscriptionId/services { taskTypeId | taskTypeName, date }` adds a service to a visit the worker has that day (priced from the subscription when it lists the type, else $0 flagged `addedBy: "worker"`; a removed one is restored, a duplicate 409). A worker acts on their own tasks (a foreman on anyone's), on today and the two days before (a foreman: 14), never on the future or an invoiced visit (409). "Today" is the company's day in `FIELD_TZ` (default `America/New_York`).
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/tasks/test.ts` ("REQ-141 generateTasks — staffed zones only, idempotent, due-only with the address snapshot, skipped not regenerated; workerView hides the price; addService priced/zero/duplicate/restore/no-visit; canAct; inActionWindow; deferTask") · integration `field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-141 the day — today's round exists on first read; generate reports unstaffed; the worker sees no price, completes with a note, un-checks, skips, restores, adds a service the office then prices, defers to tomorrow; the foreman closes another crew's task; a plain worker is 404 on another's") · e2e the story generates the day on /field/tasks and completes it on /worker.

## REQ-142 — Batch invoicing: completed, un-invoiced tasks in a date range become one DRAFT invoice per customer — through the existing invoice store — one line per task; never billed twice; sent through the existing dispatch
**Source:** the demo's REQ-012..017/037/038, kept as decided there, plus REQ-137's constraint.
**Requirement:** `POST /field/batches/pull { from, to }` (YYYY-MM-DD, from ≤ to) takes every task in the range with `status: "complete"` and no live invoice (none, or one that no longer exists or is void — the existing /invoices DELETE and void need no hook), groups them by customer, and creates one invoice per customer with `InvoiceStore.create(userId, { customerId, status: "draft", jobName, description, lineItems, amount })` — one line item per task reading "<date> — <task type> — <address>" at quantity 1 and the task's price; worker notes never carry over; each task is stamped with its invoice id; a `Batch { from, to, invoiceIds }` is recorded (none when nothing was pulled); the answer carries the batch with its invoices (read from `InvoiceStore`) and a `summary { pullable, skipped, deferred, open, alreadyInvoiced, zeroPriced }` of the range. `GET /field/batches`, `GET /field/batches/:id` list them with their invoices (missing invoices left out). `POST /field/batches/:id/send { invoiceIds: [...], allowZero? }` sends the chosen DRAFTS of that batch: email through `SendPaperworkEmail` when the customer has an email, else text through `SendPaperworkSms` when a phone; a draft with a $0 line is refused (409, the ids named) unless `allowZero`; a dispatch failure is reported per invoice, never thrown; a sent invoice is stamped `status: "sent"`, `issuedDate` today, through `InvoiceStore.update`. Editing a draft's lines, discounts, deleting it: the existing /invoices page and endpoints, unchanged — the Lotes page links to them.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/batch-lines/test.ts` ("REQ-142 linesFor — completed-in-range only; a stamped task never again; one invoice per customer with the total; the line text; the note stays out; summarize") · integration `field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-142 pull — a draft per customer readable at GET /invoices with the line items; the tasks stamped; a second pull pulls nothing; a deleted draft frees its tasks; send stamps sent and the fake dispatch is recorded; $0 refused without allowZero") · e2e the story pulls on /field/batches and finds the draft on /invoices.
**Evidence (2026-11-03):** RED — `batch-lines/test.ts` `Module not found`; then the int `REQ-137/142` assertion on `lineItems[0].description` failed because lines came in UUID order — `linesFor` now sorts by date, description, task id. GREEN — unit `6 passed`; int `REQ-142` (a draft per customer at `GET /invoices`, tasks stamped, a second pull pulls nothing, a deleted draft frees its tasks, send stamps `sent` through the fake dispatch, $0 refused without `allowZero`); the story pulls today on /field/batches and the card reads "Ana Torres · $65.00" (frame 029) with the invoice above in REQ-137's evidence.

### REQ-139/141 REVISION (2026-11-03) — PUT, not PATCH
The edit verbs read `PUT /field/subscriptions/:id` and `PUT /field/tasks/:id` — the verb this app's own paperwork controllers use (`invoice-controller` has no PATCH); the front-end client (`front-end/clients/field.ts`) calls PUT. Same bodies, same answers. The int tests name the verb they call.

### REQ-139 AMENDMENT (2026-11-03) — a missing Mapbox token never stops the app
On the real deploy `FieldGeocoder` no longer throws in its constructor when `MAPBOX_TOKEN` is unset (Danet builds every injectable at boot, so that would have taken the whole app down with the module): it logs once at boot and a subscription create/address change answers 503 "geocoding is not configured (MAPBOX_TOKEN)" until the token is set. The fake is unchanged. `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/field/` → `35 passed | 0 failed`.

## REQ-146 — Account admins: the owner invites a phone number; that person signs in with their own number and works in the owner's account
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05: "we built workers but we need admin, meaning that i type in a phone number and it invites another admin to my account. so they can sign in with their phone number and can see my data."
**Requirement:** behind the owner's session, `POST /me/admins { phoneNumber, name? }` records an admin on the account (`AccountAdmin { id, userId: the owner, phoneNumber (E.164), name?, createdAt }`) and texts the number an invite in the owner's language ("<owner> added you as an admin on DocuMonster — sign in with this number at <app url>"); the owner's own number is 400, a number already invited on this account 409, a malformed one 400; `GET /me/admins` lists them; `DELETE /me/admins/:id` removes one. Sign-in with the phone OTP (the dev code included): the person's own account is found-or-created as today, and when the number is an admin on an account the session opens IN that account — `session.userId` is the owner's id (so every `requireUser` route answers the owner's data) and `session.actorId` is the admin's own user id; the earliest invite wins when there are several; the answer carries `isNewUser: false` (an admin is not a sign-up: no CRM customer, no hello@ notice) and lands where the owner's profile says. A session that acts for an account is refused (401) the moment its admin record is gone — removal takes effect at once, no logout needed. The owner-only actions answer 403 `acting_as_admin` to an acting session: `DELETE /me`, `GET /me/wipe`, `POST /me/plan`, `POST /me/admins`, `DELETE /me/admins/:id`. `GET /me/accounts` answers `{ actor: { id, name?, phoneNumber }, currentUserId, accounts: [{ userId, label, role: "owner" | "admin" }] }` — the person's own account first, then every account they administer, labelled by business name, else owner name, else phone; `POST /me/switch-account { userId }` opens a new session in that account (own or administered, 403 otherwise), swaps the `pm_session` cookie and drops the old session. Front end: `/admins` (sidebar "Admins" / "Administradores", after Workers) — the invite form (phone, optional name) and the list with Remove; when the session acts for another account the sidebar shows "In <label>'s account" with the account switcher, and Settings hides the danger zone (the server refuses it anyway). Phone-OTP only: the email login does not look admins up.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/business/account-admins/test.ts` ("REQ-146 pickSignInAccount — own account with no memberships; the earliest invite wins; accountLabel — business, then owner name, then phone; inviteCheck — own number refused") · integration `backend/src/users/entrypoints/admins-controller/int.test.ts` ("REQ-146 the owner invites a phone (the text goes out, 201; own number 400, duplicate 409, bad phone 400); the invited phone's OTP sign-in acts for the owner: /me is the owner, /profile/identity is the owner's, isNewUser false; wipe/close/plan/admins are 403 for the admin; /me/accounts lists both; switch-account to own and back; the owner removes the admin and the acting session 401s, the next sign-in is the admin's own account") · e2e `e2e/account-admins/account-admins.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-146: the owner invites a number on /admins; a second browser signs in with that number and sees the owner's customer on /customers and the owner's business in the sidebar; the owner removes the admin").

## REQ-153 — Demo mode: a super admin guides a user through the app with a live pointer on the user's screen
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05: "we want a new feature called 'demo mode' this allows an employee to have a pointer on the users view, so it follows the screen that the user is on for the admin, and allows the user to have a pointer, when they click it does not affect the users app but has like a loud wave that you can see, this way we can help the users move through the app. it needs to be fast so its realtime so we may have to use webrtc using the hosted deno deploy as a signaliing server."
**Requirement:** A super admin (the app's only staff role — there is no employee record) starts a demo on /admin with a "Demo" button on a user's row: the backend opens a demo session for that user (`POST /demo-mode/sessions`), the admin's browser impersonates the user and lands on /dashboard as the presenter. The user's own browser learns of it on its next page load or within 30 s (`GET /demo-mode/active`) and joins as the viewer; both reconnect on every page through the one session kept in the tab. Each side sees the other's pointer on its own page — the presenter's pointer on the user's screen and the user's on the presenter's — and a click on either side is a loud expanding wave at that spot on the other screen, never an action: the overlay sits above the app with pointer events off, and the presenter's clicks, by default, are waves only (a "Point only / Interact" toggle lets the presenter act on the impersonated app). Pointers are anchored to the element under the cursor (a selector plus the fraction inside it), so a phone and a desktop show the pointer on the same button; a viewport fraction is the fallback. The presenter follows the user: the viewer reports its route on connect and on every change, and the presenter's page navigates to the same route ("Follow" is on by default, a toggle). Either side ends the demo from its pill; the demo expires on its own after two hours. Transport: both browsers hold a WebSocket to `/api/demo-mode/ws?session=<id>` on the deploy (the signaling server); the presenter offers a WebRTC peer connection (STUN only, no TURN) with an unreliable data channel for moves and a reliable one for clicks and routes; until it opens, and whenever it cannot (a symmetric NAT), the same messages ride the WebSocket as a relay, and the pill says which ("direct" / "relay"). On Deno Deploy the two sockets may land on different isolates, so the server relays through a Deno KV mailbox (`kv.watch`), not process memory; in-isolate peers are delivered directly and never twice. Access: the viewer is the demo's target user on their own session; the presenter is the demo's super admin, impersonating or not; anyone else is refused (403) on the socket and sees no demo on `active`. The root router passes a WebSocket upgrade under `/api/` to the backend with the ORIGINAL request (a re-wrapped Request breaks Deno's upgrade — proved in `compose-router` tests), so the socket controller lives at `api/demo-mode`; the dev Vite proxy forwards that path unchanged.
**Known:** the existing `/api/voice/stream` socket goes through the same re-wrap and therefore cannot upgrade on the deploy today; not changed here (its own requirement).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-mode-protocol.test.ts` ("REQ-153 …": the wire and peer messages parse and reject junk; an anchor resolves to the element's rect and falls back to the viewport; a route is followed only when it is a different same-origin path; a selector is built from an id, a data-cy or a positional path; both dictionaries carry the demoMode strings; the overlay is mounted in the shell; the admin row has the Demo button; the Vite proxy forwards the socket unchanged) · unit `backend/src/demo-mode/domain/business/demo-role/test.ts` ("REQ-153 roleFor — …") · unit `backend/src/demo-mode/domain/coordinators/demo-hub/test.ts` ("REQ-153 two hubs on one KV — a message posted in one reaches the peer joined in the other, a local peer gets it once, presence and end") · unit `compose-router.test.ts` ("REQ-153 a WebSocket upgrade under /api reaches the backend with the original request and connects; a plain /api call is stripped") · integration `backend/src/demo-mode/entrypoints/demo-mode-controller/int.test.ts` ("REQ-153 …": a super admin opens a demo for a user; the user's `active` names the presenter; a stranger sees none; the presenter's impersonation session and the user's session connect over the composed router's `/api/demo-mode/ws`; a signal and a relay cross both ways with `from`; a stranger's socket is refused; end tells both and clears `active`) · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-mode.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-153: …": the admin starts a demo from /admin; the user's browser shows the pill; the presenter's pointer and click wave appear on the user's screen; the user's move appears on the presenter's; the user opens /customers and the presenter's page follows; End clears both).
**Evidence (2026-11-05):** RED — jest `unit/demo-mode-protocol.test.ts`: `Cannot find module '../../shared/demo-mode/protocol'`; backend: `TS2307 … '#demo-mode/protocol.ts' is not defined` on all four new suites. Proved first in scratch: in Deno 2.9.7 a `Deno.upgradeWebSocket` on `new Request(url, req)` opens a socket whose first frame the client rejects ("Reserved bits are not zero") while the original request upgrades fine, and re-creating the RESPONSE (the CORS wrapper) is harmless — hence the root router's passthrough and the `api/demo-mode` controller path. GREEN — backend `deno test src/demo-mode src/core/entrypoints/compose-router` → `11 passed, 0 failed` (role rule ×5; two hubs on one `:memory:` KV: the signal crosses, the local peer has it once, presence both ways, end everywhere; leave → offline; the composed router: the upgrade connects and echoes, `/api/x` is stripped, frontend first, backend fallthrough, styled 404 last; the int suite: 403/401/404 on open, 201, `active` as viewer/presenter/nobody, a second demo replaces, the viewer ends, then the socket run — impersonation session presents, a stranger's and an unknown demo's sockets never open, welcome/peer, offer and answer and route and click cross with `from`, junk and an off-origin route are dropped, `ended` to both and both closed, no socket on an ended demo); jest `unit/demo-mode-protocol.test.ts` → `10 passed`; `shots run e2e/demo-mode` on the host (SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT 1.64.1, two browser contexts, the user's a 420×800 viewport) → `1 passed` in 4.6 s: Demo on the row → the presenter's pill "Guiding Ana Torres" on the landing page (REQ-091 lands a new account on /welcome, not /dashboard), the user's pill "Hans is guiding you" on reload, both statuses direct/relay, the presenter's move and click → `demo-pointer` and `demo-wave` on the user's screen with the presenter still on its page, the user's move → `demo-pointer` on the presenter's, /customers on the user's → the presenter's page follows, End → both pills gone and `active` null. `deno check`, `deno lint`, `deno fmt` clean on every new file. Lanes: backend unit `682 passed`; backend int `347 passed, 2 failed` and jest `712 passed, 2 failed` — the four failures are REQ-155's in-flight worker-language work sitting uncommitted in this checkout (`worker-welcome.int.test.ts`, `unit/worker-language.test.ts`), not this change.

## REQ-155 — each worker has a language, and the welcome text goes out in it
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05: "we need to be able to set the language for the worker so we know what language to send the text."
**Requirement:** A worker carries a language (Spanish or English). The add form on /field/workers picks it — Spanish by default, the crews being Spanish-speaking — and each worker's row shows it with an ES/EN switch that changes it on the spot (`PUT /field/workers/:id { language }`, the owner's). The REQ-151 welcome text (on add, and from the REQ-154 tool) goes out in the WORKER's language; a worker from before this (no language on record) falls back to the owner's, as before. The REQ-154 tool also takes `--lang es|en` to text every worker of the account in that language regardless.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/worker-welcome/test.ts` ("REQ-155 workerLang — the worker's language, else the owner's, else en") · integration `backend/src/field/entrypoints/worker-welcome.int.test.ts` ("REQ-155 a worker added with no language is Spanish and texted in Spanish by an English owner; `language: "en"` is kept and texted in English; a bad language 400s; PUT changes it and the tool then texts in the new one; the tool's `language` override texts everyone in it") · unit `jest/unit/worker-language.test.ts` (the add form's picker and the row's switch, the keys in both languages) · e2e `e2e/field-tasks/field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` (step 1: the picker reads Spanish by default, Luis's row shows ES; the row's switch to EN sticks through a reload).
**Evidence (2026-11-05):** RED — unit: `TS2305 … has no exported member 'workerLang'`; int: `0 passed | 2 failed` (no `language` in the answer, the English owner's worker texted in English, `PUT /field/workers/:id` the 404 page); jest `unit/worker-language.test.ts`: both failed (no keys, no picker, no switch, no `setWorkerLanguage`). GREEN — `FieldWorker.language?: "en" | "es"`; `workerLang(worker, owner)` and `parseLang` in `worker-welcome/mod.ts`; the create takes `language` (Spanish when absent, a bad one 400s) and the welcome goes out in `workerLang`; `PUT /field/workers/:id { language }` (the owner's worker — another account's is 403, `getOwned`'s rule as REQ-139; a bad language 400; the PIN never in the answer); the REQ-154 tool takes `language` as an override (`bad_language` otherwise) and says each row's `language`; the script takes `--lang es|en` (`✖ --lang takes en or es` on anything else) and prints the language per row; the page's add form has the picker (`wk-language`, Spanish first) and each row an ES/EN switch (`wk-row-lang`, `data-lang`) that PUTs on click. Unit `deno test -A worker-welcome/test.ts` → `3 passed | 0 failed`; `deno test -A --unstable-kv worker-welcome.int.test.ts` → `8 passed | 0 failed` three runs over; `deno task test:int` → `349 passed | 0 failed`; jest → `714 passed, 1 skipped, 715 total`; `shots run e2e/field-tasks` on the host → `4 pass · 0 fail` (`✓ REQ-143 … · 4s`: the picker reads es, Luis's row `data-lang=es`, EN clicked → `en`, still `en` after a reload); `deno fmt`, `deno lint`, `deno check` clean on every touched file. Amendments on the way: REQ-151's test now adds its worker with `language: "en"` (its English-owner expectation held only while the language was the owner's — REQ-155 supersedes that rule, the worker's own deciding, Spanish by default); the REQ-154 tests read rows by name and texts by number, because the worker list comes back in id order, which is random — the second green run of the full int suite had caught `tu PIN 2345.` where `1234.` was expected. Decisions: a NEW worker is Spanish unless the owner picks English; a worker from before (no language on record) keeps falling back to the owner's language until the row's switch sets one — so A2Z's three workers (texted in English on 2026-11-05) are English until set, or `deno task welcome-workers --business A2Z --lang es` texts all three in Spanish regardless.
**Prod (2026-11-05):** main `321ee9a` = develop `f4ae1da`'s tree, pushed 18:37:14 UTC; by 18:38:08 UTC documonster.com's dashboard sidebar read Billing / Recurring / Admin (the REQ-176 root), so this revision is the one routed. Verified alongside REQ-160..177: unit 688 + jest 732, int 368, 28 browser stories green on the combined tree.

## REQ-153 — AMENDMENT (2026-11-05): the demo is an invitation — the customer accepts in the app, then the staff browser joins them where they are
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05, testing by hand (the presenter landed on /welcome while the customer sat on /assistant with no pill until a reload): "that makes no fucking sense from a ui/ux perspective. i understand the technical reason but we need to take it to uiux."

## REQ-176 — Sidebar root: Billing holds Quotes, Invoices and Payments; Admin holds everything else but Customers
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05: "okay put payments, invoices, contracts in a folder and put all of the other stuff outside of the 'customers' in an 'admin' folder."
**Requirement:** On the REQ-156 folders, the sidebar's root is four rows: Dashboard, Customers, a "Billing" folder (`Facturación`) holding Quotes, Invoices and Payments (the quote IS the contract since REQ-… the Quote+Agreement merge, so "contracts" is the Quotes entry), and an "Admin" folder holding the rest — the Recurring folder (nested, with its five) and Admins. The super-admin operator tab sits inside the Admin folder too (as "Super admin"), not on the root. ## REQ-157 — Cadence is weekly or monthly; monthly picks days of the month on a 31-day grid, clamped to shorter months
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05: "on subscriptions the ui is off here [cadence/first-visit row]. cadence should be weekly or monthly. weekly shows mon tues wed thrus fri sat sun. monthly shows a matrix of 30 days, you can click the days. id like to do 31 days but not all months have 30 days how do we reconcile that?" … "yes show me it built out."
**Requirement:** The subscription form's Cadence offers two choices, Weekly and Monthly (a subscription saved earlier with every 2–4 weeks still shows and keeps its interval, but new ones never get it). Weekly keeps the weekday chips. Monthly shows a grid of the 31 days of the month; the owner clicks any of them (the first visit's day is picked up front), at least one is required. A subscription stores them as `daysOfMonth` (1–31, unique, sorted; `POST`/`PATCH /field/subscriptions` refuse anything else with 400). It is due on each picked day; a picked day a month does not have (29, 30, 31) falls on that month's last day, and two picks that collapse onto the same last day are one visit. Without `daysOfMonth` a monthly subscription keeps today's rule — the first visit's day, clamped. The schedule reads "Monthly · days 15, 31" / "Mensual · días 15, 31" (one day: "day 15" / "día 15"). The form says it under the grid: "29, 30 and 31 fall on the last day in shorter months." The Cadence and First visit fields sit top-aligned so their labels line up.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/schedule/test.ts` ("REQ-157 isDue — monthly on the picked days, clamped to the month's last day, one visit when two picks collapse; the old single-day rule without daysOfMonth" · "REQ-157 scheduleText — the picked days in words, singular and plural, both languages") · integration `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-157 a monthly subscription with daysOfMonth answers them sorted and unique with the schedule text; 0 or 32 is 400; a PATCH replaces them") · e2e `e2e/field-tasks/field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-157: Cadence offers weekly and monthly only; Monthly shows 31 clickable days with the first visit's day on and the short-month note; the saved card reads Monthly · days 15, 31").

GREEN — `Subscription.daysOfMonth?: number[]`; `schedule/mod.ts` `monthDaysOf` (the picks, else the start date's day) and `isDue` monthly = any pick clamped to the month's last day, `scheduleText` lists them (day/days, día/días); `parseSchedule` validates 1–31 integers, de-duplicates and sorts, on create and patch; the island's Cadence offers Weekly and Monthly (an older 2/3/4-week subscription keeps its option while edited), Monthly swaps the weekday chips for a 31-chip grid (`subs-dom-day`, `data-dom`, the first visit's day on) with the short-month note, the submit sends `daysOfMonth` and refuses none; `field.css` `.row` top-aligns (the date input is taller than the select) and `.days.dom` wraps seven to a row; `lang/*.json` `field.subs.daysOfMonth` / `field.subs.domHint`. ## REQ-158 — Cache busting: every static stylesheet and script link carries the build id
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05, after a deploy still looked old in his browser: "can you please do cache busting?"
**Requirement:** Every `<link rel="stylesheet">` and `<script src>` that points at a file under `front-end/static` is written through Fresh's `asset()` (as the landing pages already do), so the URL carries the build id (`?__frsh_c=<build>`) and changes with every deploy. The server then answers such a URL with a year-long immutable cache (`public, max-age=31536000, immutable`) while a bare URL stays uncached (`no-cache, no-store`), so a browser can never show the previous deploy's stylesheet or script next to the new page. Dynamic routes that only look like scripts (`/landing-dict.js`, a route) are left alone.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/cache-busting.test.ts` ("REQ-158 no route or component links a static .css/.js file by a bare path; every file that calls asset() imports it from fresh/runtime") · integration n/a — no backend change · e2e `e2e/cache-busting/cache-busting.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-158: the served dashboard and subscriptions pages link their stylesheets with the build id; that URL is immutable for a year, the bare one is not cached").
**Evidence (2026-11-05):** RED — jest `unit/cache-busting.test.ts`: 2 of 3 failed (53 bare links in 33 files; no asset() links at all); the story: `expectation failed: /dashboard: /welcome.css carries the build id`. GREEN — the 53 `href="/x.css"` / `src="/landing-scripts.js"` links in 33 routes and `components/LegalPage.tsx` are `{asset("/x.css")}` with `asset` imported from fresh/runtime (`/landing-dict.js`, a route, left alone); jest unit → `705 passed, 1 skipped` (two content tests that spelled the bare href — REQ-055 `head-stylesheet-keys` and REQ-152 `subs-search-select` — now match the asset() form); `deno task test:unit` → `674 passed`; `deno lint` clean; `deno check` on routes/components shows only the pre-existing AsstChat.tsx pair (file untouched). E2e on the host: `shots run e2e/cache-busting e2e/field-tasks e2e/legal-pages e2e/login-logo e2e/account-admins e2e/landing2 e2e/search-select` → `35 pass · 0 fail`. The dev server (Vite) sends no cache headers and an empty build id (`?__frsh_c=`), so the story checks the link form and the header rule only when an id is present; the header rule is prod's: before this change `curl -I https://documonster.com/dashboard.css` → `cache-control: no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate` and `…/dashboard.css?__frsh_c=9w2n9zwh0m8g` → `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. A first pass ran `deno fmt` over the whole routes dir and reformatted 11 files the fmt baseline leaves unformatted (REQ-106's content test went red on a reflowed line); reverted, and only the 22 files that were fmt-clean before were formatted.
**Prod (2026-11-05):** main `09a666c` = develop `f29652d`'s tree, pushed 15:12:24 UTC; by 15:13:07 UTC documonster.com's /login linked `verify.css?__frsh_c=g18rg4q4d86p` — that URL answers `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, the bare `/verify.css` answers `no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate`.

## REQ-170 — No Generate button: the day's tasks are always current
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05: "i dont need a generate button in tasks, just keep it up to date in realtime when subscriptions change."
**Requirement:** Reading a day — `GET /field/tasks?date=…` for the office, `GET /field/worker/tasks?date=…` for a worker — materializes that day's round first (idempotent, the same generation as before, any day, not only today), so a day is never empty for want of a click. ## REQ-171 — Texts when the day's work changes: a worker's new one-off, a customer's canceled or deferred service
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05: "send text messages to the workers if they get a new one off task for the day" · "send text messages to customers if a one off service is canceled" · "send text messages to custoemers if their service is canceled or deffered."

## REQ-153 — AMENDMENT (2026-11-05): the pointer lands on the same element on both screens, whatever the zoom, the window or the staff banner
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05, testing by hand (the customer's cursor on the assistant's green send button; the staff screen drew it at the bottom-left of the sidebar): "it needs to take scale into consideration look at this screenshot the cursor is in two different places."

The pointer's name tag flips to the left of the arrow near the right edge so it is never cut off.

## REQ-180 — The demo pointer glides: no choppy motion, the rest position always arrives
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05, testing by hand after the same-element fix: "cursor movment is a little choppy but its close."
**Requirement:** The other side's pointer moves smoothly. The sender rates its moves leading + trailing — the first of a burst goes at once, the last goes at the gap's end, nothing in between — so the position the cursor comes to rest at is never dropped (the old throttle dropped every move inside the gap, including the last). The gap is 16 ms on the data channel and 66 ms through the relay. Every move carries the sender's clock; a move that arrives after a later one (the lossy channel is unordered) is ignored, so the pointer never steps back. The receiver never snaps: the drawn pointer glides toward the latest target every frame (exponential approach, 50 ms time constant, settles exactly on the target, never overshoots), written to the element directly rather than through state and a CSS transition.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-mode-motion.test.ts` (the gaps; the throttle's leading send, one trailing send carrying the LAST value at the gap's end, cancel; `newerMove`; the parser keeps a finite `t` on a move and drops junk; `glideStep` approaches every frame on a straight line, never overshoots, settles on the target in a few frames, no time → no motion, a long gap → at once; the overlay imports the module, sends through the throttle with `t: performance.now()`, drops late moves, glides via `style.transform`, has no CSS transition and no transform in the style string) · integration n/a — no HTTP change · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-mode.e2e.test.ts` (the user reaches the privacy link with a thirty-move sweep whose last move follows the previous within the gap; the presenter's pointer passes through ≥ 12 distinct positions, never steps back, and RESTS inside the presenter's privacy link box).
**Evidence (2026-11-05):** RED — jest: `Cannot find module '../../shared/demo-mode/motion.ts'`; e2e: `expectation failed: the presenter's pointer (115.095,634) sits on the presenter's privacy link {"x":495.4375,…,"width":102.65625,…}` — the burst's final moves were dropped and the pointer rested 380 px short. GREEN — `shared/demo-mode/motion.ts` (`moveThrottle`, `glideStep`, `newerMove`, the constants), `shared/demo-mode/protocol.ts` (`t?` on the move message, kept by the parser), `DemoModeOverlay.tsx` (`throttle` via `useMemo`, `glideTo`/`hidePointer`/`frame`, the pointer element painted through a ref); jest demo files → `25 passed`; jest unit project → `757 passed, 1 skipped`; `shots run e2e/demo-mode` on the host → `✓ REQ-153 + REQ-179 + REQ-180: … · 7.1s` (see the line above for the exact time of the final run); check/lint/fmt clean. ## REQ-182 — Over text, the pointer sits on the same character on both screens, whatever the zoom or the line wrap
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05, after the screen recording of the staff Safari at ~2.5× zoom beside the customer's Chrome (the staff cursor at the end of the heading "zona.", the customer's pointer on the paragraph beneath): "fix it."
**Requirement:** When the pointer is over text, its anchor names the character under it: the browser's caret under the point gives a text node and an offset; if that character's box is on the pointer's line (within half a line above or below), the anchor carries the element path of the text's parent, the text node's index among that element's own text nodes (`ti`) and the character offset (`ci`), besides the box fraction. The other side puts the pointer on that same character's box — its centre, or its right edge for the caret after the last character — so "after zona." lands after "zona." on a one-line heading and on a four-line one alike, and a sweep across a paragraph follows the words. Empty space on a line snaps to the nearest glyph; a point farther from any line, and anything that is not text (the map, a button), keeps the box-fraction rule. A page that lacks the character falls back to the box, then the viewport.

## REQ-185 — On a map, the pointer sits on the same ground on both screens, whatever the map box, zoom or pan
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05, the screen recording of the customer's Safari beside the staff Chrome on /field/assignments (the staff pointer tens of pixels off on the map, on top of US 501 while the customer's cursor was west of it): "look at the last screen recording." → "how do you fix it?"
**Requirement:** Leaflet's tiles take no pointer events, so the element under a cursor on the map is the map container, and a fraction of that box names different ground when the two boxes differ in size (the same centre and zoom, a 744×560 box beside a 500×380 one: 49 px east, 18 px south — measured). ## REQ-186 — In the space between elements, the pointer keeps its distance from the nearest element — no jump at an element's edge
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05, the screen recording after REQ-185 (the staff Safari beside the customer's Chrome on /field/assignments): "id dyou not se the cursor on the right do some wierd up/down behavior?" — measured: five moments where the staff cursor rises through the gap above the map while the customer's pointer sinks 40 px into the map, then races up.
**Requirement:** A point in a layout gap hits a container (the page's content box, a grid) whose box is taller on one side than the other (wrapped text, one column instead of two), so its box fraction lands elsewhere — just above the map on one side was 40–90 px inside the map on the other, and the pointer reversed direction at the edge. Instead: when the element under the point has sized element children and the point is inside none of them, the anchor names the NEAREST child (by distance to its box) with the fraction inside that child's box clamped as before plus the overshoot beyond its edges (`ox`, `oy`: the distance outside the box as a fraction of the box's size, each within ±1, kept by the parser only with a selector). The other side places the pointer at that child's box plus the overshoot — just above the map here stays just above the map there, and moving away from an element moves the pointer away on both screens. Ground on a map (REQ-185) and a character in text (REQ-182) still come first; a point farther than one box-size from every child keeps the container's box fraction.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-mode-gap-anchor.test.ts` (the parser keeps `ox`/`oy` within ±1 with a selector and drops junk, out-of-range and selector-less ones; `placeAnchor` adds the overshoot; `nearestRect` picks the closest box by edge distance, inside = 0; `outsideFrac` splits a point into the clamped fraction and the overshoot; `anchor.ts` asks `gapBox` after the caret rule and before the box fraction) · integration n/a — no HTTP change · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-mode.e2e.test.ts` (on /field/assignments the user rests 6 px above their map; the presenter's pointer sits above the presenter's map, within 40 px of its top; the user moves 10 px higher and the presenter's pointer moves higher too).
**Evidence (2026-11-05):** The recording, tracked frame by frame (the orange name tag on the customer's screen against the staff's native cursor): at 0.30 s the staff cursor rose 34 px per 0.1 s through the gap above the map while the pointer sank 40 px into the map, then raced up 100 px per 0.1 s to catch up; the same at 1.15 s, 2.20 s, 3.05 s and 3.95 s. RED — jest `5 failed, 5 total` (`nearestRect is not a function`); e2e `expectation failed: REQ-186: the presenter's pointer (y 301.831) sits just above the presenter's map (top 343.03125)` — the container's fraction put it 41 px off. GREEN — `shared/demo-mode/protocol.ts` (`Anchor.ox/oy`, the parser's ±1 rule, `nearestRect`, `outsideFrac`, `placeAnchor` adds the overshoot), `front-end/lib/demo-mode/anchor.ts` (`gapBox`, asked after the caret rule and before the box fraction); jest file → `5 passed`; jest demo files → `41 passed`; jest unit project → `776 passed, 1 skipped`; `shots run e2e/demo-mode` on the host → `✓ … + REQ-185 + REQ-186: … · 11.8s`; fmt/lint/check clean on the touched files. ## REQ-182 — AMENDMENT (2026-11-05): the character rule works on the presenter's side too — the caret lookup must see past the overlay's own layers

## REQ-187 — Demo mode: the customer's screen is the truth — the staff side shows a scaled replica of it
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05 ("put a grid on each at normal size, figure out where the grid is zoom wise and viewport wise, scale it and then move on the grid"; "the person using the app is the source of truth, that becomes what the app becomes on our screen"; "point only is fine"). After a day of per-case anchoring rules (REQ-182/185/186) each recording showed a new misplacement — the two pages were never the same picture (184 px sidebar vs 52 px rail, a heading wrapped on 4 vs 5 lines, different ground on the map).
**Requirement:**
- The presenter's browser does not show its own layout of the app. Clicking Demo on /admin impersonates the customer (as before) and opens `/demo/stage`: a dark stage with ONE frame — the app, as the customer, rendered at EXACTLY the customer's layout viewport in CSS px (their width × height) and scaled, keeping aspect, to fit the staff window. Same viewport → the same media queries → the same layout → the same pixels at a different scale.
- The customer's app is the source of truth and reports its view over the demo link: viewport width/height (on join and on resize), the page (pathname + search, on every change), every scrolled element's scroll position (window and inner scrollers such as `.content`, named by the same positional selector as REQ-153 AMENDMENT), the sidebar's collapsed flag and mobile-drawer flag, and the map's centre and zoom on /field/assignments. The stage applies each: it navigates the frame, scrolls the same elements, and hands page-local state (sidebar, map) into the frame. On join the customer sends the whole view; after that, patches.
- Inside the replica frame the app runs as the customer sees it: no impersonation banner, no demo overlay of its own (the frame never polls `active`, never joins the link); the sidebar and the map take their state from the stage instead of local storage / their own fit.
- Point only. A transparent layer covers the frame: the presenter's pointer moves and clicks are sent as viewport fractions and never reach the frame. There is no Follow toggle and no Interact toggle any more (REQ-153 AMENDMENT below); the pill carries the customer's name, the link status, the frame size ("{name}'s screen, w × h") and End. End (either side) hands the presenter their own account back (stop-impersonating → /admin) as before.
- Before the customer's app joins, the stage shows the frame at a default phone viewport on the customer's last reported page (REQ-153 AMENDMENT — same screen at once), the pill saying "Waiting for {name} to accept…"; the first view report resizes it.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-mode-replica.test.ts` (REQ-187: `parsePeerMessage` accepts a `view` patch and drops junk fields; `fitScale` fits the customer's viewport inside the stage keeping aspect; the stage route and island exist, the frame is named `pm-demo-replica`, has pointer events off, and sits under the capture layer; the overlay sends the presenter to `/demo/stage` and is inert inside the frame; the banner, the sidebar and the map read `isReplicaFrame`; the sidebar and the map report their state) · integration n/a (the backend is untouched: the relay already forwards any parsed peer message) · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-mode.e2e.test.ts` (the presenter lands on `/demo/stage`; the frame is 420 × 800 like the user's window and on the user's page; inside it there is no banner and no demo pill; the user's sidebar and the frame's sidebar have the same width and the user's privacy link and the frame's privacy link the same box; the user scrolls `.content`, opens the drawer, changes page and pans the map — the frame follows each).

## REQ-189 — A stale island module never wedges a page: dev modules are never cached, and a page whose island code fails to load reloads itself once
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05 ("the employee is wedged. can you fix that and prevent it from happening again?"). Measured in the staff Safari on /welcome: the page's module graph still held `fresh-island::DemoModeOverlay` served from Safari's cache (0 bytes transferred, no revalidation, although Vite answers `Cache-Control: no-cache` + ETag) and that old copy imported `/lib/demo-mode/anchor.ts`, deleted by REQ-188 → the import failed → no island on the page hydrated (the wizard, the banner, the overlay all dead). A plain reload did not refresh it; a `cache: "reload"` fetch of the island URL followed by a reload did.
**Requirement:**
- The dev server (Vite) serves every transformed module — islands, `fresh:client-entry`, project files — with `Cache-Control: no-store`, so a browser can never reuse island code from before an edit. (Vite's own `no-cache` + ETag relies on revalidation, which the staff's Safari did not do.) Pre-bundled dependencies keep Vite's immutable caching.
- The app shell carries a recovery script on every page: when the page's module script or an island import fails to load (Safari: "Importing a module script failed."; Chromium/Firefox: "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module" / "error loading dynamically imported module"; or the module `<script>`'s error event), it refetches every module the page loaded with `cache: "reload"` and reloads the page — once per tab session (`sessionStorage` "pm:module-reloaded"), so a page that is really broken never loops.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/module-recovery.test.ts` (the Vite plugin maps `no-cache` to `no-store`; the shell's script has the guard, the refetch, the three messages, both listeners, and is part of the boot script) · integration `jest/integration/dev-modules-no-store.int.test.ts` (the running dev server answers `no-store` for `/@id/fresh:client-entry` and an island file) · e2e `e2e/module-recovery/module-recovery.e2e.test.ts` (the first request for the login island is made to fail; the page reloads itself exactly once and the login form is live; the guard is set).
**Evidence for REQ-189 (2026-11-05):** The wedge, measured live in the staff Safari on /welcome: `fresh-island::DemoModeOverlay` served from the browser's cache (0 bytes transferred) and importing the deleted `/lib/demo-mode/anchor.ts` (failed load); the overlay, banner and wizard islands dead. A plain `location.reload()` left it so; `fetch(url, {cache: "reload"})` of the island and the client entry, then a reload, brought the page back (the overlay then polled `active?path=/welcome`). RED — jest unit `4 failed` (no plugin, no recovery script); jest integration `cache-control` expected `no-store`, received `no-cache`; e2e `REQ-189 … waitForFunction: Timeout` (no reload). GREEN — `front-end/vite.config.ts` plugin `pm-dev-no-store` (wraps `res.setHeader`, `no-cache` → `no-store`; checked with curl on `/@id/fresh:client-entry`, `/islands/LoginForm.tsx`, `/lib/i18n.ts`); `front-end/routes/_app.tsx` `MODULE_RECOVERY_SCRIPT` on the boot script (a first version had a regex-escaping syntax error that broke the whole boot script — caught by a headless Chromium probe and `node --check` of the served script, fixed before any test went green); jest unit project `86 suites, 774 passed, 1 skipped`; jest integration `dev-modules-no-store` `4 passed`; `shots run e2e/module-recovery e2e/demo-mode` → `✓ REQ-189 … 3.2s` (the login island aborted for the first load; the page reloads itself once, the guard is set, the form takes input; with the island aborted again the guarded page does not reload) and `✓ REQ-153 + … + REQ-188` still green; fmt/lint clean. Dev server restarted (Vite config). Not reproducible in the e2e: Safari's own cache behaviour (Chromium revalidates) — the live measurement above is the Safari evidence.

## REQ-189 — AMENDMENT (2026-11-05): the recovery reload is limited to once per 30 s per tab, not once per tab
A once-per-tab guard made the safety net single-use: a later, genuine failure in the same tab would never recover. The guard is now a timestamp in sessionStorage; a second failure within 30 s does not reload (no loop), one after that does. Tests: the same three, updated in place.

## REQ-189 — AMENDMENT 2 (2026-11-05): on a dev host every load checks the modules' ETags and reloads once when the page ran stale code
**Source:** the measurement that followed the first amendment: with `no-store` (and even `Vary: *`, `Pragma`, `Expires`) Safari still served the replica frame's sidebar island from its cache on a frame reload (0 bytes, the edited module's marker absent) — Safari reuses module scripts across navigations whatever the headers say; only a `fetch(url, {cache: "reload"})` from that window refreshes its copy. A once-per-browser purge therefore fixes the past, not the next edit.
**Requirement:** On localhost / 127.0.0.1, after every page load, the shell refetches each module the page loaded bypassing the cache (refreshing Safari's copy), records each ETag in the tab (sessionStorage "pm:module-etags"), and compares with the previous load's: any change means the page just ran stale code, so it reloads once under the same 30 s cooldown. The once-per-browser purge is replaced by this. Production (hashed assets) is untouched.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/module-recovery.test.ts` (AMENDMENT block rewritten) · integration n/a · e2e `e2e/module-recovery/module-recovery.e2e.test.ts` (second story: the client entry's remembered ETag is seeded wrong; the next load reloads itself once, remembers the real ETag, and does not reload again).
**Evidence (2026-11-05):** unit `jest --selectProjects unit` → 86 suites, 776 passed, 1 skipped (module-recovery block rewritten: load listener, `cache:"reload"`, ETag map in `pm:module-etags`, 30 s cooldown, no `pm:modules-purged`). e2e `shots run e2e/module-recovery` → ✓ "a module whose ETag differs … reloads itself once and remembers the new ETags" (2.8 s) and ✓ REQ-189 login-island story (3.2 s); `shots run e2e/demo-mode` ✓. Live in Safari's stage tab (`/demo/stage`, replica frame on `/assistant`): sidebar island stamped with a marker → stage reloaded → frame reports the marker (`pmSb: 5`, 65 333 bytes over the wire, not 0 from cache); marker removed → reloaded → marker gone (64 561 bytes). The served `_app` boot script was saved and passed `node --check`. The `Vary: *` / `Pragma` / `Expires` experiment was reverted (no effect on Safari; `no-store` + ETag stay).

## REQ-183 — Google Tag Manager on every page, behind GTM_ID
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05: "install this" — Emily Keck's (monsterrg.com) install instructions, forwarded again by Hans: Google's container snippet "as high as possible inside `<head>`, on every page" and the `<noscript>` iframe "right after the opening `<body>` tag, on every page"; "Please respond back when its install so I can build out our other reports." The thread carries the placeholder container id `GTM-XXXXXXX`, not the real one.
**Requirement:** every page the app serves carries Google Tag Manager: Google's inline container snippet verbatim (the `gtm.start` push onto `dataLayer`, then the async `gtm.js?id=<container>` loader inserted before the first script) as the first script in `<head>`, right after the charset meta, and the `<noscript>` iframe for `ns.html?id=<container>` as the first thing inside `<body>`. The container id is NOT a constant: the thread has a placeholder, so it comes from `GTM_ID` (`.env.example`), validated as `GTM-` + letters/digits — anything else counts as unset, so a typo can never reach the inline script. Which loader follows REQ-124/REQ-080 (REQ-318: the fakes): Google's on the real deploy (`DENO_DEPLOY` or `DENO_DEPLOYMENT_ID` set) with `GTM_ID` set; nothing on the real deploy without it (tag management never takes the site down); the app's own `/gtm-fake.js` (it only marks `<html data-gtm-loaded="fake">`) on the gate, a dev box and a pin, under `GTM_ID` when set or the placeholder container `GTM-FAKE000` when not — so a test run never lands in the container's reports. The `<noscript>` iframe points at Google only in real mode (there is nothing to fake for a browser without scripts). The Google tag of REQ-124 stays as it is; GTM is added beside it.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/google-tag-manager.test.ts` ("REQ-183 the snippet is Google's, verbatim, with the container id and the loader in it; the noscript iframe url"; "REQ-183 which loader: Google's on the real deploy with GTM_ID, nothing on the real deploy without it, the fake elsewhere; an id that is not GTM-… is unset"; "REQ-183 the app shell carries it on every page: first script in the head, the noscript first in the body; the fake exists and never talks to Google") · int: n/a — two scripts in the front-end's shell, no backend seam · e2e `e2e/google-tag-manager/google-tag-manager.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-183: every page carries Google Tag Manager — the container snippet first in the head, gtm.start on the dataLayer, the loader fetched; on the real deploy the noscript iframe first in the body": /, /login, /privacy, /landing2 — on fakes the fake's mark on `<html>`; with `DENO_DEPLOY=true` and a `GTM_ID` the request for Google's gtm.js for that container and the noscript iframe as the body's first child).
**Evidence (2026-11-05):** RED first — `npx jest unit/google-tag-manager.test.ts`: `Cannot find module '../../shared/google-tag-manager/gtm'`; `shots run e2e/google-tag-manager` with no implementation: `locator.waitFor: Timeout 15000ms exceeded` on `head script[data-gtm]` (16.4 s). Then GREEN — jest: 3 passed; the story on fakes: 1 pass (1 s, 4 pages: /, /login, /privacy, /landing2 — snippet first in the served head, `gtm.start` first on the dataLayer, `/gtm-fake.js?id=GTM-FAKE000` requested, the fake's mark on `<html>`); the same story against `PORT=5391 DENO_DEPLOY=true GTM_ID=GTM-TEST123 deno task serve` (`BASE_URL`, `DENO_DEPLOY=true`, `GTM_ID` for the story): 1 pass (1.2 s) — the served page opens `<head><meta charset="utf-8"/><script data-gtm="real" nonce=…>(function(w,d,s,l,i){…` and `<body><noscript><iframe src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/ns.html?id=GTM-TEST123"`, Google's `gtm.js?id=GTM-TEST123` requested on each page, the noscript the body's first child; a real-deploy serve WITHOUT `GTM_ID`: /privacy 28 025 bytes, 0 matches for `data-gtm|ns.html|/gtm.js|gtm-fake`, REQ-124's gtag still there. ## REQ-198 — Account and document numbering: every client has its own number, every document its own sequence
**Source:** Hans Pedersen, 2026-11-06 00:30 ("DocuMonster: Numbering, linked documents, and versions before A2Z onboarding"): "Each client has a unique identifying number. Under that client: customers, quotes, invoices, contracts, change orders, work orders. Records are separate for each client, so two clients can both have customer 001 or INV-001. Sequences default to 001. … Once numbers are issued they are never reused."
**Requirement:** Every account gets a permanent account number (`DM-0001`, one global counter, assigned on first use, shown on the profile). Every customer, quote, invoice, change order and work order carries a document number from its own per-account sequence (`C-001`, `Q-001`, `INV-001`, `CO-001`, `WO-001`; at least three digits, growing as needed) and a `seq`. Sequences are per account and per kind: two accounts both have an INV-001. A number is taken in the same atomic transaction that stores the record (compare-and-set on the counter), so a number can never be issued twice and a record is never stored without consuming its number; a deleted record's number is not reissued. Everything that names a document (dashboard lists, public pages, PDFs, emails, SMS, receipts, exports, search) uses the number, never an id slice.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/document-numbering.test.ts` ("REQ-198 formats every kind…", "REQ-198 docNumberOf…") · integration `backend/src/core/data/doc-numbering/int.test.ts` (per-account/per-kind counters, 250 concurrent allocations with no duplicate and no gap, a refused write commits nothing), `backend/src/paperwork/domain/data/numbered-docs.int.test.ts` (quotes/invoices/customers/change orders numbered per account) · e2e `backend/src/users/entrypoints/numbering-controller/e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-198/199: GET /profile/numbering shows the account number…"), browser stories of REQ-201/205/206 assert the numbers on screen.

## REQ-199 — Starting numbers in Settings, set once; a setup reset before going live
**Source:** Hans, 2026-11-06: "Settings lets the client choose the starting number for each sequence before the first document is created (Q-001, INV-5000). Starting numbers are set once. A setup reset clears test records and restarts numbering before going live. Once live, numbering is locked and advances."
**Requirement:** Settings → "Document numbering" shows the account number and, per kind, the next number and an editable starting number (integer ≥ 1). `PUT /profile/numbering` stores the starts; once a kind has issued its first number that kind is locked (409 `numbering_locked`, the input disabled with a lock note), other kinds stay settable. "Reset test data" (danger zone, house modal, no window.confirm) → `POST /me/setup-reset` (owner only) deletes every record of the account — customers, quotes, invoices, change orders, work orders, payments, conversations, files — and every sequence and idempotency key, keeps the account, session, profile, plan, settings and account number, and the starts become settable again; numbering restarts at the chosen starts.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/document-numbering.test.ts` ("REQ-199 starting numbers are parsed strictly…"), `jest/unit/numbering-settings.test.ts` (REQ-199: the PUT patch from the form, lock notes) · integration `backend/src/core/data/doc-numbering/int.test.ts` (starts honoured, reset) · e2e `backend/src/users/entrypoints/numbering-controller/e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-199: starting numbers are honoured… locked once that kind has issued", "REQ-199: POST /me/setup-reset clears the account's records and counters, keeps the account…; another account is untouched"), browser `e2e/settings-numbering/settings-numbering.e2e.test.ts`.

## REQ-200 — Creating a document is idempotent and atomic: retries and simultaneous creates never duplicate numbers or documents
**Source:** Hans, 2026-11-06: "Simultaneous creation or retries must not create duplicate numbers or duplicate documents." A2Z may send hundreds of invoices in November.
**Requirement:** `POST /customers`, `/quotes`, `/invoices`, `/invoices/:id/change-orders`, `/work-orders` accept a `requestId` (body) or `Idempotency-Key` header; a retry with the same id returns the first document, no second number. The number allocation is a compare-and-set on the per-account counter inside the record's own transaction, serialized per (account, kind) in-process and retried across isolates, so concurrent creates get consecutive distinct numbers. The front end sends one `requestId` per form submission. Public decisions are compare-and-set too: accepting a quote or deciding a change order twice (two tabs, a double tap) wins once and answers 409 `already_accepted` / `already_approved` / `already_declined` the second time.
**Tests:** unit n/a — KV semantics, covered at integration · integration `backend/src/core/data/doc-numbering/int.test.ts` (250 concurrent, refused write commits nothing), `backend/src/paperwork/domain/data/numbered-docs.int.test.ts` ("requestId idempotency", "updateIf applies once") · e2e `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/revisions-controller/e2e.test.ts` (REQ-200 concurrent accept), `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/work-order-controller/e2e.test.ts` (retry returns the same document).

## REQ-201 — Versions: a published revision keeps the number and the link, advances the version, keeps every version
**Source:** Hans, 2026-11-06: "Show the version number near Draft / Final. Publishing keeps the number and the link and advances the version. … 'Q-001 · Version 3 · Accepted and Signed · [Date]' … 'INV-5000 · Version 2 · Revised invoice — replaces previous version'. One permanent customer link. 'Publish revision and notify customer' … Old links keep working. Draft edits don't change the live document until published. Keep all versions internally with who and when, no purging."
**Requirement:** Every numbered document has `version` (from 1), `publishedAt`, `publishedBy` (who: the signed-in person, an acting editor, or the customer for a customer-driven change like an approved change order). Editing a draft applies live. Editing an issued quote/invoice stores the content fields as `pendingRevision` (the live document and its link are unchanged; the dashboard shows "Unpublished changes"); `POST /quotes/:id/publish` / `POST /invoices/:id/publish` `{notify}` moves the pending content live as version N+1 on the same id, number and link, files version N (`["doc_version", kind, id, N]` with its content, who published it and when it was superseded — never purged), and with `notify` re-sends the same link by email/SMS. Sending a document with unpublished changes publishes them first. `GET …/:id/versions` lists every version. The version and state are shown next to the number on the dashboard, public pages, PDFs and emails ("Version 2 · Revised invoice — replaces previous version").
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/document-numbering.test.ts` ("REQ-201 versionOf… applyRevision…", "REQ-201 editing an issued quote goes pending…", "REQ-201 document states"), `jest/unit/invoice-form.test.ts`, `jest/unit/linked-documents.test.ts` (labels) · integration `backend/src/paperwork/domain/data/numbered-docs.int.test.ts` ("publishRevision + versions filed") · e2e `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/revisions-controller/e2e.test.ts` (REQ-201 pending → publish → version 2, versions listed, draft edits live), browser `e2e/invoice-numbering/invoice-numbering.e2e.test.ts`, `e2e/linked-documents/linked-documents.e2e.test.ts`.

## REQ-202 — Locks: signed quotes and paid invoices are final; unpaid invoices stay revisable with partial payments preserved and overpayment flagged
**Source:** Hans, 2026-11-06: "After signing … preserved and locked; later scope changes go through change orders. … invoices revisable until fully paid; preserve partial payments; flag overpayment; paid invoices locked; same for signed contracts and approved change orders."
**Requirement:** An accepted (signed) quote refuses content edits (409 `locked_signed`); scope changes after signing are change orders, which are numbered, never expire, are part of the agreement's record, and keep who approved them (`approvedName`, `decidedAt`). An invoice is revisable until fully paid: a revision keeps `paidCents`, recomputes the balance against the new amount, and sets `overpaidCents` when payments exceed it (shown as an "Overpaid" flag on the dashboard, the public page and the PDF — never hidden); an invoice whose balance reaches zero becomes `paid` and is locked (409 `locked_paid` on edit, delete, discount, new change order). An approved change order is locked as approved; editing it re-opens approval as a new version.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/document-numbering.test.ts` ("REQ-202 an invoice is revisable until fully paid…", "REQ-202 balances keep partial payments and flag overpayment…") · integration `backend/src/paperwork/domain/data/numbered-docs.int.test.ts` (change orders: index, no expiry) · e2e `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/revisions-controller/e2e.test.ts` (REQ-202 locked_signed, locked_paid, partial payment kept across a revision, overpaid flagged), `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/e2e.test.ts` (change-order approval on a paid invoice refused).

## REQ-203 — Nobody signs or pays against an outdated page
**Source:** Hans, 2026-11-06: "Prevent signing an outdated version. Check the current balance before taking payment, even from an old page. Customer edits must not rewrite issued documents."
**Requirement:** The public quote page carries the version it rendered; accepting sends it, and a quote that was republished since answers 409 `stale_version {currentVersion}` — the page reloads the latest version and the customer signs that one. A payment claim sends the balance it showed (`amountCents`) and the version; the server recomputes the balance from confirmed payments and answers 409 `stale_balance {balanceCents, version}` when it differs (the page shows the current balance) and 409 `already_paid` when nothing is owed; the recorded intent is the server's balance. A customer's acceptance/approval never rewrites the issued content: it only stamps the decision (status, signature, name, date).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/linked-documents.test.ts` (REQ-203 stale handling) · integration n/a — HTTP-level · e2e `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/revisions-controller/e2e.test.ts` (REQ-203 stale_version, stale_balance, already_paid), browser `e2e/linked-documents/linked-documents.e2e.test.ts`.

Exports carry the document number, version, customer number, related numbers, addresses, dates, amounts and status, so an accounting import can match a revised invoice to the earlier export by number and version.

## REQ-189 — AMENDMENT (2026-11-06): the dev-host module refetch releases every response it opens
**Source:** the full browser lane on the a2z-docs tree: nine signup stories (REQ-080/082/083/089/091/121/147/148) failed with `page.waitForLoadState: Timeout 90000ms exceeded` on /welcome; the same story failed the same way on develop e4a58f9 in the main checkout. A probe story that tracked `request` vs `requestfinished` on /welcome after signup listed ~60 requests still open 8–12 s after load — every one a module URL (`/@id/fresh-island::…`, `/@fs/…`, `/lib/i18n.ts`, …): the AMENDMENT's after-load refetch (`fetch(u,{cache:"reload"})`, d226b76) read the ETag header and never read or cancelled the body, so Chromium kept each response open and the page never went network-idle. (Prod is unaffected: that refetch only runs on localhost/127.0.0.1; the error-path `recover()` had the same leak but reloads the page anyway.)
**Revision:** both refetches in `MODULE_RECOVERY_SCRIPT` (`front-end/routes/_app.tsx`) cancel the body once the headers are read (`drain(r)`: `r.body.cancel()`). No product change.
**Tests:** e2e the nine stories above + `e2e/module-recovery` (unchanged, still green) · unit `jest/unit/module-recovery.test.ts` (unchanged, still green) · int n/a.
**Evidence (2026-11-06):** probe before: `PROBE pending-count=60` (12 s old from /landing2, 8 s from /welcome); after the fix: `PROBE pending-count=0`. Then `shots run e2e/meta-pixel e2e/dev-code e2e/landing2-motion e2e/landing2 e2e/onboarding-until-answered e2e/landing3 e2e/landing4 e2e/module-recovery e2e/sidebar-folders` → `40 pass · 0 fail`; the full lane → `119 pass · 0 fail`.

## REQ-211 — Every landing form says which landing page and which ad it came from
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-06 ("There is a way to see where someone fills out a form to for a call back, or a demo or a signup? There is something that says what landing page it is coming from?" — "can you make it so plz? can you make it so the answer is yes?").
**Finding:** No. The signup posted the phone and the language only, the demo/call-me posted the booking only, the contact form its five fields; the CRM lead's source was the constant "paperworkmonster.com" for everyone; the demo email's heading hardcoded "/landing2"; the `?ad=` id only swapped the hero photo.
**Requirement:** Every public landing form (the OTP signup on / and /landing2–5, the demo booking and the call-me card → POST /demo-request, the contact form → POST /contact) also posts `page` (the browser's pathname) and `ad` (the `?ad=` id, when there is one). The server normalizes them into a lead origin (`shared/lead-origin/mod.ts`: a path of at most 80 safe characters, an ad id of at most 40; anything else is dropped, never refused). The origin rides the lead to the CRM: the lead's source reads "paperworkmonster.com · /landing5?ad=cumple" (the base stays "paperworkmonster.com" when no page is known); it survives the outbox's retries; a brand-new account born from that signup keeps it (`user.origin`, stamped once at creation, never writable through PUT /me), so every later profile sync says the same source. The demo/call-me team email says the page in its heading and in a "Page" row; the contact email gets the same row.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/business/lead-origin/test.ts` (the normalizer), `backend/src/communication/domain/business/demo-request/test.ts` (REQ-211 cases: the page and the ad parsed, junk dropped, the email names the page), `jest/unit/lead-origin.test.ts` (the landing client attaches the page and the ad from the browser's location; the home page's signup script posts them) · integration `send-otp/int.test.ts` (the OTP record carries the origin), `verify-otp/int.test.ts` (a new account is born with it; an existing one is untouched), `crm-capture-outbox/int.test.ts` (add keeps it, defer keeps it), `crm-lead-capture/int.test.ts` (the sweep hands it to the CRM), `crm-customer-sync/int.test.ts` (the lead's and the account's source name the page), `auth-controller/int.test.ts` (POST /auth/send-otp with page+ad → the CRM door sees the source), `demo-request-controller/int.test.ts` and `contact-public-controller/int.test.ts` (the email and the lead carry it) · e2e `e2e/lead-origin/lead-origin.e2e.test.ts` (on the fakes: /landing5?ad=sabado's call-me posts page "/landing5" and ad "sabado"; /landing2's signup posts page "/landing2" and no ad; the home page's signup posts page "/").

## REQ-214 — Demo mode: several staff present at once, each with their own name and colour
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-06: "can you add multiple demo'ers with thier name and a different color to demo mode this way we can have any staff running on that."
**Requirement:** Any super admin can run a demo, and more than one can run the SAME demo at once: a staff member who clicks Demo on a customer who is already being guided joins that demo as another presenter (same session, 200) instead of being refused or starting a second one; a presenter who opens a demo for a different customer leaves the first (it goes on for the others, and ends only when its last presenter leaves). Every presenter carries their name and a colour of their own, taken from a fixed palette of distinct colours (the first presenter keeps the green the demo always had; none of them is the customer's orange), handed out so that two presenters in one demo never share one. The customer's screen draws one pointer per presenter — the arrow, the waves and the name tag in that presenter's colour — and the pill names them all; each staff stage draws the customer's pointer and the other presenters' pointers in their colours and lists who is presenting with their colour dots. Over the wire every presenter's message is stamped with who sent it (`pid`), presence says which presenter came or went, and a presenter can address the other presenters only (their pointer rides to the customer directly and to colleagues through the relay). End, from anyone, still ends it for everyone.

## REQ-218 — Every public page names its one canonical URL, and the web manifest names only icons that exist
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-10, forwarding Google Search Console's notice of 2026-11-09 to Andy ("New reasons prevent pages from being indexed on site documonster.com": Duplicate without user-selected canonical · Not found (404) · Blocked by robots.txt · Page with redirect): "i got This email about this site."
**Cause, from prod on 2026-11-10 (curl against https://documonster.com):** (1) `/contact`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/sms-terms` and `/refund-policy` each answered 200 at three URLs — bare, `?lang=en`, `?lang=es` — with no `<link rel="canonical">` (the five landings and "/" had one); the footer and the language toggle link the `?lang=` forms, so a crawler finds all three. (2) `/manifest.webmanifest`, linked from every page, named `/icon-192.png`, `/icon-512.png` and `/icon-maskable-512.png`; all three answered 404 and no commit ever added them (`git log --all -- 'front-end/static/icon-*'` is empty). The other two reasons are the site working as written: robots.txt has disallowed `/login`, `/verify`, the app and the customer documents since `ee6f1a6` (2026-08-18), and the redirects are http→https and the signed-out app pages (`/dashboard`, `/verify`, `/welcome` → 302). They are "new" because the property is: the site moved to documonster.com on 2026-10-18 (REQ-085).
**Requirement:** `/contact` and the four legal pages carry exactly one `<link rel="canonical">`, the bare path on `SITE_ORIGIN`, whichever language the request asked for; every page the sitemap lists has one. Every icon `manifest.webmanifest` names is a file in `front-end/static/`, a PNG of the size the manifest declares (192, 512, maskable 512 — cut from the site's own `monster-paper.png` on the manifest's background colour, the maskable one inside the safe zone).
**Not changed (decisions, not defects):** robots.txt; the sitemap; the landings' `hreflang` alternates, which point at `?lang=` URLs whose canonical is the bare page (so only the Spanish default of each landing is indexable). Outside the repo: the old domain's forwarder answers 404 for every path but "/" and forwards "/" to `http://`; `www.documonster.com` resolves but has no certificate.

## REQ-219 — Every path on a retired host lands on the same path of the site
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-10, after REQ-218, on what it takes for Google Search Console's notice to be resolved ("Not found (404)", "Page with redirect"): "Okay, well, you do that."
**Cause, from the internet on 2026-11-10 (curl):** the old domain was a registrar forwarder — `/` answered 301, every other path (`/login`, `/pricing?x=1`) answered 404, so every old link in a text, an email or a search result was dead; and `https://www.documonster.com/` resolved to the app's address but had no certificate.

The list of retired hosts is one shared constant (`shared/site-host/retired.ts`), names only — nothing in the repo links to the old domain (REQ-086 stands).
**Outside the repo, needed for it to take effect:** the three hosts added as domains of the Deno Deploy app (certificates), and the old domain's DNS pointed at the app instead of the registrar's forwarder.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/retired-hosts.test.ts` ("REQ-219 …": the three retired hosts; path and query kept; case, port and trailing dot; the site, previews, localhost and look-alikes left alone; `//other.example` stays a path; the rule is the app's first middleware, ahead of `staticFiles()`, and answers 301) · integration `jest/integration/retired-hosts.int.test.ts` ("REQ-219 …" over the dev stack with a raw Host header: five retired-host requests each 301 to the same path on the origin; the site's own host served 200) · e2e n/a — a browser cannot name a host that does not resolve to the test server; the live proof is the prod line below, taken with curl once DNS points at the app.
