REQ-218: `/contact`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/sms-terms`, `/refund-policy` × bare/`?lang=en`/`?lang=es` — 15 of 15 carry exactly one canonical, the bare URL; `/icon-192.png`, `/icon-512.png`, `/icon-maskable-512.png` answer 200 image/png; all seven sitemap pages answer 200 with a canonical. REQ-219: the rule is deployed but NOT yet reachable — the three retired hosts are not domains of the Deno Deploy app (a TLS request naming one is refused), and the old domain's DNS still points at the registrar's forwarder, which was changed the same day to send `/` to `https://documonster.com/` in one hop (deep paths still 404 there).

## REQ-220 — Settings: "Transfer account" next to the phone — a new number takes the account, and that person owns it
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11 ("a phone number is not editable … because the phone number is the identifier … I would like to have a button next to that that says transfer account that allows you to put a different phone number in, changes the phone number, and now that person owns the account.").
**Requirement:** On Settings → Account the phone row carries a "Transfer account" button. It opens a dialog: the new owner's phone number, then a 6-digit code texted to THAT number (its own text, naming the account — not the sign-in code), typed back into the dialog. A right code moves the account: the user's `phoneNumber` and the phone index change in one atomic write, so the new number signs in to this same account (same id, every record, the plan, the admins) and the old number no longer does — a later sign-in on the old number is a brand-new account. The owner's own sessions are dropped (this browser lands on /login); an admin's sessions stay; if the new number was an admin of this account that invite is removed (it is the owner now). The CRM customer is re-synced with the new phone. Refused: the owner's current number (`same_number`, 409), a number that already has an account, open or closed (`phone_taken`, 409 — at the start and again at the atomic write), an unusable number (`bad_phone`, 400), a resend inside 30 s (`cooldown`, 429), a wrong code (`invalid_code`, 422 — not 401, which the signed-in app reads as a dead session and leaves for /login; five wrong codes lock it, `rate_limited`, 429), no pending or an expired code (`expired`, 410; codes live 10 minutes). Owner only: an admin acting for the account gets 403 and never sees the button. Off the real deploy the reply carries the code (`devCode`, as REQ-082) and the dialog shows it.
**Decision, mine (not asked for):** the code to the new number. Without it a mistyped digit hands the account — customers, documents, the Stripe keys — to a stranger, with no way back from Settings.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/business/transfer-account/test.ts` (the pure rules: the refusals, which sessions are the owner's own), `jest/unit/transfer-account.test.ts` (the settings card carries the button on the phone row, hidden while acting; the dialog's two steps, the client's two calls, the redirect; both languages carry every key) · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/transfer-account/int.test.ts` (start texts the new number its own code and stores it; the refusals; confirm moves the record and the index, frees the old number, drops the owner's sessions and keeps an admin's, removes the new owner's admin invite; wrong / expired / locked codes; a number taken between start and confirm), `backend/src/users/entrypoints/me-controller/transfer.e2e.test.ts` (the app booted: start → devCode → confirm; the old session is 401; the new number's sign-in is the same account; the old number's is a new one; an admin is 403; the statuses) · e2e `e2e/transfer-account/transfer-account.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-220: …" in a browser: the button on the phone row, the dialog, the code, the bounce to /login, the new number sees the old owner's customer).
**Evidence (2026-11-11, local, REQ-220):** RED first — `deno test` on the three backend files → "Type checking failed" (TS2307, the modules did not exist); `jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern transfer-account` → "Test Suites: 1 failed" (ENOENT `front-end/components/TransferAccount.tsx`). GREEN, on a clean worktree of origin/develop `5390bb9` carrying this change alone — `deno task test:unit` → "ok | 729 passed | 0 failed" and jest "Test Suites: 98 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 895 passed, 896 total"; `deno task test:int` → "ok | 417 passed | 0 failed"; `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/users/entrypoints/me-controller` → "ok | 18 passed | 0 failed"; `shots run e2e/transfer-account e2e/account-admins e2e/settings-numbering` → "3 pass · 0 fail". One thing the browser lane caught: the wrong code first answered 401, and `front-end/client.ts` sends a signed-in page to /login on any 401 from /api (net log: `POST /api/me/transfer/confirm 401` → `GET /login?next=%2Fsettings`) — so `invalid_code` is 422. `deno check` + `deno lint` clean on the touched front-end files, `deno lint` on the touched backend files.

**Prod (2026-11-11) for REQ-220:** main `103d67a` (develop `a88a008`'s tree, byte-identical) pushed 21:09:50 UTC; `POST https://documonster.com/api/me/transfer/start` answered 404 at 21:09:45 and 21:10:26 UTC and 401 at 21:10:42 UTC (the route exists, no session); the served dictionary chunk `/assets/i18n-DmC-kFk5.js` carries `"settings.transfer.button":"Transfer account"` and `"Transferir cuenta"`.

## REQ-242 — Demo mode: the stage is a live mirror of the customer's actual screen, not a second copy of the app (supersedes REQ-187's replica; amends REQ-188)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11: "fix every issue the demo found" — the 20-agent demo's stage and pointer findings B1, M1, M4, M5, M6, M7, M9, M10, M12, M20, stage-content-m1, stage-content-p1, pointer-and-replica-side-effects-m1, -m2, -polish1, -pair4. Root cause (demo-rca.md, cluster "demo-mirror", analyst + skeptic, at fb6d4fa): REQ-187's stage is an independent live copy of the app — the iframe `pm-demo-replica` loading the customer's URL under the presenter's impersonation — linked to the customer only by a small View (size, path, scrolls, sidebar flags, map). It can never show island state (the assistant's flow past the first bubble, dialogs, typed text, toasts, card flips), a reload of the same URL, data saved on the same page, or the language; it runs the app's mount-time writes as the customer (PUT quote, sample-quote, run-nudges, translate); it waits on a made-up 390 × 844 phone at start; and its pointer fractions land on whatever the stale copy has there.
**Requirement:**
- The stage shows a mirror of the customer's actual document. The customer's app (the demo overlay) records its document: a full snapshot (elements, text, attributes, input values and checked states, scrolls, canvas bitmaps, the viewport, the page) when a presenter joins, on every page load (a reload of the same URL included — each load is a new snapshot), and whenever a stage asks (`resync`); then the changes, batched about every 50 ms: nodes added, removed and moved, attributes, text, input values (typed or set by code), scrolls, the viewport, the URL (pushState/replaceState).
- The frames ride the existing demo link — the WebRTC data channel, the WebSocket relay when it is not open — as `dom` chunks of at most 16 000 characters (a frame over 4 KB is gzip-compressed first), each tagged with its page-load id and sequence number. The stage reassembles them, applies the frames strictly in order, and asks for a fresh snapshot when one has been missing for 2 s or a frame does not fit what it holds.
- The stage replays them into ONE frame that runs no script: `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` (never `allow-scripts`), a srcdoc document whose Content-Security-Policy forbids scripts, frames, objects, media and connections. It never runs the app: no SSR, no API calls, no writes as the customer, no pixel, nothing written to the staff browser's storage. The frame is the customer's real viewport (width × height) scaled to fit; until the first snapshot arrives the stage says "Connecting to {name}'s screen…" — no invented phone frame, no page the customer is not on. A snapshot's scrolls are applied again once its styles and images are in (an element only scrolls once its stylesheet has loaded).
- Never mirrored: scripts, `<noscript>`, the demo overlay (`data-demo-overlay`), the staff banner (`data-demo-skip`), comments, preload/prefetch links, `http-equiv` metas, tracking pixels; an embedded frame is an empty box (never loaded). Password inputs, one-time-code inputs (the sign-in code, a worker's PIN) and anything under `data-demo-mask` are masked (•).
- The customer's app is inert in a nested frame: the welcome wizard's quote preview never joins the demo, never draws a second pill, never reports its page.
- Pointers: a move or a click carries the viewport fraction and, when there is one, the mirrored node under it (its mirror id and the point's fraction of that node's box); the receiver puts the pointer on that node when it has it, at the fraction otherwise. The presenter's resting pointer is sent again when the customer's page (re)joins and after every new snapshot; a presenter who leaves has their pointer cleared on the customer's screen; the customer's pointer on the stage is hidden on a new page and when the customer's app disconnects, and the customer's app sends `leave` on pagehide. The name tag flips to stay inside the frame's box (stage) or the window (customer) and fades after 1.5 s without movement; the arrow dims after 6 s. A move's clock is its sender's page clock (`performance.now()`, which starts over on every page load), so a receiver forgets a sender's clock whenever that sender's page changes (the customer's page joins, drops, or a new page load is mirrored; a presenter comes or goes) — the moves of the next page are never dropped as stale.
- Point only, and End from either side, stand (REQ-187/188/153). The replica is removed: the `pm-demo-replica` frame, `isReplicaFrame`, `reportView`/`onReplicaView`/`requestViews`, the View patch, the positional selectors, the default phone view.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-mode-mirror.test.ts` (REQ-242: the `dom`/`resync` messages and the node anchor parse, junk dropped; chunking and reassembly in any order; frames applied in order, a gap held and then stalled into a resync, a snapshot resetting the order; gzip encode/decode; the name tag's placement inside a box), `jest/unit/demo-mode-mirror-dom.test.ts` (REQ-242 on a fake DOM: a snapshot replays scripts/noscript/overlay/comments out, inputs masked, URLs absolute, iframes empty, SVG namespaced; a chat bubble, a dialog with typed text, attribute/text changes, moves and removals replay incrementally; 300 random mutation rounds — the incrementally replayed DOM equals a fresh snapshot's every round; scrolls the replay lost are taken again on `settle()`; an unknown id is a desync; node anchors both ways), `jest/unit/demo-mode-mirror-wiring.test.ts` (REQ-242: the stage's frame is sandboxed without scripts and has a CSP, no replica left anywhere, the overlay inert in nested frames, the pointer lifecycle wired, the move clocks forgotten with the sender's page, the stage settling a snapshot's scrolls); amended for REQ-242: `jest/unit/demo-mode-protocol.test.ts` (the `view` message parses to null; the `shouldFollow`/selector tests went with the code; the stage never uses `targetPath`), `jest/unit/demo-mode-motion.test.ts` (a move is `anchorOf({ x, y })` — the fraction plus the node); removed with the replica: `jest/unit/demo-mode-replica.test.ts` · integration `backend/src/demo-mode/entrypoints/demo-mode-controller/int.test.ts` ("REQ-242 …": a 120 KB snapshot crosses the composed router's relay as `dom` chunks and reassembles byte-identical on the presenter; a presenter's `resync` reaches the viewer; oversized or malformed chunks are dropped), `backend/src/demo-mode/domain/coordinators/demo-hub/test.ts` ("REQ-242 …": full-size chunks cross two isolates through the KV mailbox intact, every one once, and reassemble byte-identical whatever order they come in — the mailbox orders the mail of one millisecond by its random id) · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-mirror.e2e.test.ts` (REQ-242 in two browsers: connecting first, then the frame at the customer's exact viewport; the customer types in the assistant composer, sends, opens Settings → Transfer account and types a number — the stage shows the bubble, the dialog and the typed text; ES on the customer turns the stage Spanish; a reload of the same URL re-mirrors; a nested app frame on the customer's page draws no second pill; the presenter's resting pointer reappears on the customer's next page; the customer's pointer leaves the stage on a new page; the staff browser sends no write to /api and loads no app module while mirroring), `e2e/demo-mode/demo-mode.e2e.test.ts` and `e2e/demo-mode/demo-presenters.e2e.test.ts` (amended to the mirror: the same steps, the frame read through the stage).

**Evidence (2026-11-11, branch fix/demo-mirror off develop 53f3cfc):** RED first — `npx jest --selectProjects unit` on the three new suites → "Test Suites: 3 failed, 3 total · Tests: 10 failed" (no `mirror.ts`, no `mirror-record.ts`/`mirror-replay.ts`, the replica still wired); `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/demo-mode/` → "Found 16 errors" (TS2307 no `shared/demo-mode/mirror.ts`, TS2305 no `MIRROR_CHUNK_CHARS`, TS2322 `"resync"` not a peer message); on a pristine worktree of develop 53f3cfc `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-mirror.e2e.test.ts` → "locator.waitFor: Timeout 15000ms … waiting for [data-cy='demo-connecting']" (the stage showed the made-up phone), and the amended `demo-mode` / `demo-presenters` stories → "timed out: the stage is connecting, or already mirrors the customer's page" / "Hans's frame is on Ana's page — expected "/welcome", got null". Two more reds came up on the way and were fixed test-first: the mirror story's pointer-m2 step ("timed out: the stage shows the customer's pointer" — every move of the customer's new page was dropped because the stage kept the old page's `performance.now()` clock; wiring test red "1 failed", then the clocks reset with the page) and the late-styles scroll (`settle()`, "2 failed" → green). GREEN on the branch — jest unit lane "Test Suites: 100 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 917 passed, 918 total" (the 300-round random walk included); `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/demo-mode/` → "ok | 18 passed | 0 failed" (the two REQ-242 relay tests 10/10 each on repeat); `src/core/entrypoints/compose-router/` → "ok | 2 passed"; `deno check` on every touched island, lib and route → no errors; `deno lint` → "Checked 15 files"; `deno fmt --check` on the 24 touched files → clean (all were clean on develop); `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-mirror.e2e.test.ts e2e/demo-mode/demo-mode.e2e.test.ts e2e/demo-mode/demo-presenters.e2e.test.ts` → "3 pass · 0 fail" (the mirror story green four runs in a row, the amended two three). The story saves the two screens side by side (`mirror-1-stage-assistant.png` / `mirror-1-customer-assistant.png`, `mirror-2-stage-dialog.png` / `mirror-2-customer-dialog.png` in its evidence folder): the stage shows the customer's styled page, the bubble, the Transfer dialog with the typed number, and the customer's pointer and click wave.

## REQ-232 — Demo mode: every customer tab and every staff window is its own connection — the stage follows the tab the customer is using, never freezes on "waiting", says plainly whether it is live, and "Return to your account" really returns
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11: "fix every issue the demo found" — the 20-agent demo (demo-report.md) issues B3 (a second customer tab takes over the stage; closing it freezes the stage on "Waiting for … to accept…"), demo-lifecycle-m1 (the staff pill says "Waiting for … to accept…" at the start and flashes it on every customer page change), demo-lifecycle-m3 (a second window of the same staff account joins silently; the customer sees one pointer for both), demo-lifecycle-p1 ("direct" / "relay" are jargon and the two sides often disagree) and M21 ("Return to your account" during a demo bounces the staff straight back to the stage). Root causes: demo-rca.md, "demo-lifecycle".
**Cause (demo-rca.md, re-checked on develop 53f3cfc):** the hub and the stage treated "the customer" as ONE yes/no flag, not a set of sockets — every customer socket that closed sent an unnamed "viewer offline", which tore WebRTC down and showed "waiting" even with another tab live (`demo-hub/mod.ts` leave/presence, `transport.ts` peer handling); a stage's offer went to every tab and the stage merged every tab's view, last write wins; identity was per user, not per socket, so two windows of one staff account shared one connection key, one pointer and one address; any page of a presenting staff account that polled `/active` re-impersonated and jumped to the stage (`DemoModeOverlay` check → placePresenter), which is what bounced "Return to your account" (it never left the demo) and pulled a second window onto the stage; the pills printed the transport mode ("direct"/"relay") and a leftover consent line ("Waiting for {name} to accept…") although the customer is never asked (REQ-153 AMENDMENT auto-join).
**Requirement:** (1) Every demo socket — each customer tab, each staff stage — has its own connection id (`cid`), stamped by the server on its welcome, its presence and everything it sends; a signal can be addressed to ONE socket. (2) A stage keeps the SET of the customer's tabs: it shows "waiting" only when no tab is left, and only after a short grace (5 s) so a page change in the customer's app (a new page = a new socket) never flashes it. (3) The stage follows ONE tab — the one the customer used last: a tab claims it when it loads in front, comes to the front, gets focus or is clicked; when the followed tab closes, the stage falls back to the tab used most recently and asks it for its whole view; the other tabs' messages never reach the stage. (4) One stage per staff account: a newer stage of the same account takes over, and the older window says so ("Open in another window", with "Use this window"). (5) A page of a presenting staff account never moves itself onto the stage: only the tab that clicked Demo is placed; any other page shows "Guiding {name}" with "Back to the demo". (6) "Return to your account" during a demo asks first and then takes the staff member out of the demo (POST `/demo-mode/sessions/:id/leave`: the demo goes on for the other presenters and ends when its last presenter leaves) before handing their account back — it lands on /admin and stays there. (7) The pills say plainly whether the demo is live: the customer "Connected" / "Connecting…", the staff "Live" / "Connecting…" / "Waiting for {name}'s app…" — never "accept", never "direct" or "relay" (`demoMode.direct`, `demoMode.relay`, `demoMode.waiting` are gone from both dictionaries); both sides read it from the server's presence, so they agree.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/demo-mode/domain/coordinators/demo-hub/test.ts` ("REQ-232 …": two tabs arrive and leave under their own cids; an addressed signal reaches one tab; a claim reaches the stages with its cid and a sync one tab; a second stage of one account replaces the first, in the same hub and across hubs; cross-hub replies are addressed by cid), `jest/unit/demo-mode-viewers.test.ts` (the wire messages parse; the transport with a fake socket — a tab leaving while another is there never shows "waiting", a page change inside the grace never shows it, the stage follows the claiming tab and drops the others' messages, falls back and syncs when the followed tab leaves, addresses its offer to one tab, a customer keeps one connection per stage even for two windows of one account, a replaced stage stops for good, a tab re-claims after a reconnect and for a new stage; the dictionaries and the islands' wiring) · integration `backend/src/demo-mode/entrypoints/demo-mode-controller/int.test.ts` ("REQ-232 …" over the composed router's socket: two tabs' cids, an addressed signal, one tab closing while the other stays, the claim; `POST …/leave` — 403 for the customer, a presenter with a colleague leaves and the demo goes on, the last one ends it; a second stage of the same account replaces the first) · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-viewers.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-232 …": a second customer tab is followed, a click in the first takes the stage back, closing the second never freezes the stage; a page change never shows the waiting line; the pills say Live / Connected and never accept/direct/relay; a second window of the same staff account stays on /admin with "Back to the demo", taking over tells the first window; "Return to your account" asks, leaves the demo and stays on /admin).
**Evidence (2026-11-11, local, worktree on develop 53f3cfc):** RED first, before any fix — `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/demo-mode/domain/coordinators/demo-hub/test.ts` → "FAILED | 3 passed | 4 failed" ("the stage's socket has an id of its own", "window 1 is told it is replaced", "timed out: the stage hears both tabs (the replies), by cid"); the controller int test → "FAILED | 5 passed | 3 failed" (welcome without a cid, `…/leave` 404 where 403 was wanted: "the customer ends a demo, never leaves it", presence `cid: undefined`); `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern demo-mode-viewers` → "Tests: 17 failed, 17 total" (B3: expected "relay", received "waiting"; m1: `["relay","waiting","relay"]`; `t.link.claim is not a function`); `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-viewers.e2e.test.ts` → "0 pass · 5 fail" — B3 "timed out: B3: a click in tab 1 takes the stage back (420 × 800)", m1 `["direct","relay","Waiting for Ana Torres to accept…","relay","Waiting for Ana Torres to accept…","relay","direct"]`, m3 `expected "/admin", got "/demo/stage"`, p1 `("Waiting for Ana Torres to accept…")`, M21 "pages after it: /admin → /admin → /demo/stage → /demo/stage". ## REQ-225 — The client's "open" counts only the client: the owner, an acting admin and staff (the demo replica) record no view and never flip sent → viewed
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11, on the 20-agent demo report: "fix every issue the demo found". Demo issues **M18** ("Contractor previews and the replica count as client 'opens' / 'Viewed by the client'") and **test-setup-claims-m3** ("Opening the public quote link as the owner, or through the staff demo stage, flips the quote sent → viewed and records a customer 'open'"); RCA in `demo-rca.md`.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked on develop 53f3cfc):** `GET /quotes/:id/public` (`backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/mod.ts`, `getQuotePublic`) never looked at the session: every load wrote a view row and flipped a `sent` quote to `viewed` with a `viewed` bus event. So the contractor's "view as customer" tab, the /welcome sample-preview iframe (owner cookie, the sample is created `sent`) and the demo stage's replica frame (an impersonation session following the customer to /q/:id) all counted as the client opening it.
**Requirement:** The public quote page still serves everyone, but a request whose session is the quote owner's (their own, or an admin acting for the account) or any impersonation session (staff, the demo replica) records no open and leaves the status alone. A request with no session, or a session from another account, is the client: it records the open and the first one flips sent → viewed, as before.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/paperwork/domain/business/internal-viewer/test.ts` ("REQ-225 …": no session counts; owner, acting admin and impersonation don't; another account does) · integration `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-225 public e2e …", the app booted: owner via `x-session-id`, owner via the `pm_session` cookie the /api proxy forwards, and an impersonation session each leave the quote `sent` with 0 opens; the anonymous GET then flips it to `viewed` with 1 open) · e2e n/a — the decision is made by the backend from the session alone, and the integration test drives the exact request the /q page sends (the Fresh `/api` proxy forwards every request header, the cookie included); a browser story adds no path the booted-app test does not cover.
**Evidence (2026-11-11, branch fix/public-views off develop 53f3cfc):** RED first — the unit test would not load (TS2307, `internal-viewer/mod.ts` did not exist); the integration test failed on the owner's own GET: `AssertionError: Values are not equal. - viewed + sent`. GREEN — `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/business/internal-viewer src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller` → "ok | 29 passed | 0 failed"; neighbours `deno test -A --unstable-kv --parallel src/paperwork src/analytics` → "ok | 352 passed | 0 failed", `src/demo-mode src/agents/domain/coordinators/ensure-sample-quote` → "ok | 16 passed | 0 failed"; `deno lint` + `deno check` clean on the touched files.
## REQ-229 — CompleteRegistration is the account's own: never a staff login, never a staff member impersonating the account (the demo stage's frame)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11: "fix every issue the demo found". Demo issues `test-setup-claims-pixel-staff-registration` ("CompleteRegistration fires for staff logins and from the staff's demo stage frame; the real pixel would do the same in production") and `demo-lifecycle-m4` ("The waiting frame on /welcome fires the 'CompleteRegistration' pixel from the staff impersonation"), root cause in demo-rca.md: `front-end/routes/welcome.tsx` rendered `<MetaPixelEvent event={registrationEvent(user.id)} />` for every signed-in session with a question open — no check for a super admin or an impersonation — and the once-per-browser guard is a localStorage key in the STAFF's browser, so the stage's replica frame (same origin, impersonating the customer) counted `reg:<customerId>` from the staff's browser (demo pairs 4, 9/10).
**Requirement:** REQ-080's CompleteRegistration ("a new account reached /welcome") fires only for a person on their own account. /welcome asks the session's context (`GET /admin/whoami`, in process) and renders the event only when that says authenticated, not a super admin, not impersonating (`shared/meta-pixel/pixel.ts` `registrationEventFor`, applied by `front-end/lib/pixel-registration.ts`); a context it cannot read sends nothing (fail closed). Inside the demo stage's replica frame (`window.name` `pm-demo-replica`, framed) the pixel neither boots (no init, no PageView) nor fires any conversion, and spends no once-per-browser key. The pixel still boots for staff on the funnel pages; only the registration is withheld.

**Evidence (2026-11-11, branch fix/pixel-registration off develop 53f3cfc):** RED first — jest `meta-pixel-registration.test.ts` 5/5 failed (`registrationEventFor is not a function`; the frame's script still called `fbq("track","CompleteRegistration"…)`; the boot threw on `document` in the frame; welcome.tsx still had the unconditional event); `deno test lib/pixel-registration.test.ts` → TS2307 (module missing); the int test → type check failed (`registrationEventFor` not exported); the e2e story with the fix stashed → "expectation failed: a staff login is not a registration — expected 0, got 1". ## REQ-226 — A text that can't reach a phone on file says "check the number", never "add their phone", and never shows Twilio or 21211
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11, on the 20-agent demo: "fix every issue the demo found". Demo issues `quote-invoice-money-m4` ("'Add their phone to deliver' although a phone was given"), `test-setup-claims-555-copy` (the fictional-number copy ships to production with Twilio jargon, and its "21211" sets off the add-phone card) and `customers-payments-fieldops-m1` (Twilio error code "21211" shown to the contractor). The root-cause analysis is in `demo-rca.md`.
**Cause (RCA at fb6d4fa, re-checked on develop 53f3cfc):** the send result carried only a translated sentence. `AsstChat.tsx` (two sites) chose the recovery card with `/Invalid|21211/i.test(smsFailureReason)`, a regex written for Twilio's raw error (c2b7c2c). The REQ-030 copy `sms.fictionalNumber` ("…(Twilio would reject it: 21211)", 0589b6e) matched it, and the card had one phone headline: `asstChat.recovery.addPhone`, "Add their phone to deliver". All four `sms.*` failure strings in en and es named Twilio and its code.
**Requirement:** a failed text carries a structured `failureCode` (`missing` | `invalid` | `fictional` | `notMobile` | `optedOut` | `other`). It is set on every failure in `SendPaperworkSms` and copied to the send-quote divider as `smsFailureCode`. The assistant's recovery card decides from that code (`shared/quote-flow/sms-failure.ts` `smsRecoveryAsk`), never from the reason text:
- no phone on file → "Add their phone to deliver"
- a phone on file that is invalid, fictional or not a mobile → "That number can't get texts — check it" / "Ese número no recibe mensajes — revísalo", with the number on file pre-filled
- opted out or any other failure → no phone card

A divider stored before the code existed, with a phone on file, gets no phone card. The four `sms.*` failure strings (en + es) name neither the provider nor an error code; those stay in `detail` and the logs.
**Tests:**
- unit `jest/unit/sms-failure.test.ts` ("REQ-226 …"): the add/check/none decision, including the demo case; the reason-key → code mapping; neither dictionary carries Twilio or a 2XXXX code in the four strings; both carry the new headlines; AsstChat no longer has the regex and calls `smsRecoveryAsk`.
- integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/send-quote/int.test.ts` ("REQ-226 …"): a fictional 555-01XX phone gives `smsFailureCode: "fictional"` with plain copy in the reason and the divider; no phone gives `missing`; Twilio's own 21211 gives `invalid` with plain copy.
- e2e `e2e/sms-recovery/sms-recovery.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-226 (en|es) …"), in a browser: a quote texted to a customer whose phone is (512) 555-0123 → the card asks to check the number, pre-filled, and "Twilio" and "21211" appear nowhere on the page.

**Evidence (2026-11-11, local):**
- RED first. jest unit → "Cannot find module '../../shared/quote-flow/sms-failure.ts'". The three backend tests → "AssertionError: Values are not equal … Actual undefined" (no `smsFailureCode`). With the fix stashed, the e2e stories on a dev stack at PORT=57431 → `✗ REQ-226 (en) … expectation failed: the card asks to check the number: "Add their phone to deliver"` and `✗ REQ-226 (es) … "Agrega su teléfono para enviar"`, which is what the demo saw.
- GREEN. `deno task test:unit` → "ok | 729 passed | 0 failed", and jest "Test Suites: 99 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 906 passed". `deno task test:int` → "ok | 417 passed | 0 failed". `shots run e2e/sms-recovery` → "2 pass · 0 fail".
- `deno check` on the touched backend files is clean, and `deno lint` on the touched files is clean. `deno check islands/AsstChat.tsx` reports the same two TS errors at line 3507 (`ClientsPageResponse.find`) as develop does without this change.
## REQ-227 — A skipped onboarding question is deferred: the dashboard opens, the next code asks again; staff never meet the customer wizard
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11, on the 20-agent demo: "fix every issue the demo found." Demo issues **M2** ("Dashboard always redirects to /welcome — 'Add your logo'"), **test-setup-claims-nc-dashboard** ("Not covered: dashboard and setup checklist — blocked by the /welcome redirect loop") and **demo-lifecycle-p2** ("Staff admin is sent through the customer onboarding, and their own /admin row has a Demo button"); root-cause analysis in `demo-rca.md` (analyst + skeptic, both UPHELD).
**Cause (RCA, re-checked at develop `53f3cfc`):** `front-end/routes/dashboard/_middleware.ts` sent every account with any of REQ-091's nine questions open to `/welcome` (302), and a wizard step's Skip was only `ctx.advance` — nothing was saved — so an account without a logo (or insurance) could never open `/dashboard`; the sidebar's Dashboard link looped to "Add your logo — Step 1 of N", and the dashboard's SetupChecklist could never render. `welcome.logo.why` / `welcome.insurance.why` (en, es) still said "Optional step … You can do this later from your dashboard" because REQ-091's copy test read only the `*.question` keys. The gate had no exception for staff (`superAdmin`), so a staff login went through "Paso 1 de 10" and its CompleteRegistration pixel; `AdminPage` drew Impersonate and Demo on the admin's own row, and `POST /demo-mode/sessions` accepted the admin's own id.
**Decision (made by the orchestrator, not by Raphael — keeps REQ-091):** onboarding keeps asking until every question is answered (REQ-091 stands), but a step's Skip now saves a per-question "deferred" stamp; the `/dashboard` gate lets the person through when every open question is deferred (the sign-in landing still brings them back to the wizard to ask again). Staff (super admin) accounts are never sent through the customer wizard, and their own `/admin` row has no Demo button.
**Requirement:** (1) A wizard step's Skip posts `POST /api/me/onboarding/deferred { question }` before it moves on; the backend stamps `user.onboardingDeferred[question] = now-ISO` (`UserStore.deferOnboarding`, the only write path — never through `PUT /me`). Every question but the name can be deferred (`DEFERRABLE_QUESTIONS`; the name step has no Skip); the name or anything that is not a wizard question is a 400. (2) One rule, `shared/quote-flow/onboarding-questions.ts`: `dashboardBlockers` = the open questions not deferred, none for staff; the dashboard's gate (`dashboardGateQuestions`) reads it — empty lets the person in, and its setup checklist asks for what is left. A deferred question is still open: `signInLanding` sends the next code to the wizard, which asks it again. (3) `isStaff` (`user.superAdmin`): a staff code lands on `/dashboard?welcome=back`, the dashboard never redirects staff, `/welcome` sends staff to `/dashboard`. (4) `/admin`: the signed-in admin's own row offers neither Impersonate nor Demo (`AdminPage selfId`), and `POST /demo-mode/sessions` with the admin's own id is a 400 with no demo opened. (5) `welcome.logo.why` / `welcome.insurance.why` (en, es) no longer call the step optional: "Skip it for now and we'll ask again next time — your dashboard keeps it on your setup list."
**Amends:** REQ-091 — "the dashboard brings the wizard back while a question is open" now reads "while a question is open and not deferred, for a customer account"; the code verify and the wizard's own rules are unchanged. REQ-091's copy test is extended to every `welcome.*.why` key.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/onboarding-questions.test.ts` ("REQ-091 + REQ-227: … the question AND its *.why line"; "REQ-227: …", 8 — the deferrable list, deferral opens the dashboard but not for the name, deferred still lands the code in the wizard, staff, and the pages read the rule: the gate, /welcome, the wizard's Skip, the admin's own row) · `backend/src/users/domain/data/user-store/smk.test.ts` ("REQ-227 user-store smoke: deferOnboarding …") · integration `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/sign-in-landing/int.test.ts` ("REQ-227 sign-in-landing — a deferred question still lands the code in the wizard; a super admin lands on the dashboard") · `backend/src/demo-mode/entrypoints/demo-mode-controller/int.test.ts` ("REQ-227 a super admin may not open a demo on their own account: 400, and no demo is open") · `backend/src/users/entrypoints/me-controller/e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-227 me e2e: POST /me/onboarding/deferred …": the stamp, 400 for the name/unknown, no session rejected, `PUT /me` cannot smuggle one) · e2e `e2e/onboarding-until-answered/onboarding-until-answered.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-227: the logo skipped in the wizard is deferred — /dashboard opens with the setup checklist asking for it; the next code lands in the wizard at the logo again"; "REQ-227: staff are never sent through the customer wizard — a super admin's code lands on the dashboard, /welcome lets them go, and their own /admin row has no Demo or Impersonate").
**Evidence (2026-11-11, local, worktree `fix/dashboard-gate` off develop `53f3cfc`):** RED first — jest unit "Tests: 8 failed, 5 passed" (`DEFERRABLE_QUESTIONS is not iterable`, `dashboardBlockers is not a function`, `isStaff is not a function`, the `*.why` copy matched /optional/, the pages' patterns missing); `deno test --filter REQ-227` on the four backend files → "0 passed | 4 failed" (`deferOnboarding is not a function`; the self-demo answered 200 with a demo id; the deferral route did not exist); shots on a `PORT=5917 deno task serve` stack → both REQ-227 stories failed: "a deferred logo no longer bounces the dashboard — expected "/dashboard", got "/welcome"" and "a staff code lands on the dashboard, not the wizard — expected "/dashboard", got "/welcome"". GREEN — jest unit project "Test Suites: 98 passed; Tests: 1 skipped, 903 passed"; `deno test -A --unstable-kv` over me-controller, user-store, sign-in-landing, load-profile, auth-controller, signup-progress and demo-mode → "ok | 88 passed | 0 failed"; shots `e2e/onboarding-until-answered` → "5 pass · 0 fail" (REQ-091 ×2, REQ-121, REQ-227 ×2). Front-end `deno lint .` / `deno check` show the same 22 problems / 8 type errors as develop `53f3cfc` without this change (none in the files touched here).
## REQ-224 — The payment ticker names the client, the money in dollars, and the method as a word
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11: "fix every issue the demo found" — demo issues **M36** (the ticker read "Tu cliente pagó 45000": cents, no currency, no client name) and **i18n-formatting-m14** (the claim line read "… dice que pagó por zelle": the raw lowercase method). Root cause (demo RCA, analyst + skeptic UPHELD): `ConfirmPayment` emitted `invoice:paid` with `amount: intent.amount` (INTEGER CENTS) and no `customerName`; `NotifyOnEvent` dropped that number straight into `notify.invoice.paidAmount`; the public claim emitted `method: dto.method` (the enum) and `notify.invoice.claimedVia` printed it raw. Titles are re-rendered from stored params on every read, so stored rows stayed wrong.
**Requirement:** A confirmed payment's feed line names the customer and the amount as money — "María Pérez pagó $450" / "María Pérez paid $450" — and a claim names the method as a word in the viewer's language — "… dice que pagó por Zelle", "… pagó en efectivo" / "… paid via Zelle", "… paid in cash". The money and the method are formatted when the line is rendered (from `amountCents` and the method enum), so rows already stored with the raw cents or the raw enum read correctly too. "Stays after confirmation" is the feed being a history (the claim happened) — not changed.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/communication/domain/coordinators/notify-on-event/test.ts` ("REQ-224 …": `amountCents` renders as dollars in en/es; a stored row with numeric cents re-renders as dollars; a claim's method renders as its localized phrase for every method; a stored raw-enum row re-renders) · integration `backend/src/communication/domain/coordinators/notify-on-event/int.test.ts` ("REQ-224 …": the producers' real payloads through the EventBus into the store, localized in es and en) · e2e `backend/src/communication/entrypoints/notification-controller/e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-224 …": the booted app — a customer claims by Zelle on the public invoice, the contractor confirms, GET /notifications in Spanish reads "María Pérez dice que pagó por Zelle — …" and "María Pérez pagó $450"). Browser e2e n/a — the ticker prints `/notifications` titles verbatim; the API-level e2e asserts those exact strings.
**Fix:** `ConfirmPayment` emits `amountCents` (named as cents) and the client's name as the bill shows it (REQ-204 snapshot); `NotifyOnEvent` stores `amountCents` and the raw `method`, and formats both when it renders a line (`renderParams`: cents → "$450"/"$1,234.50"; a legacy numeric `amount` is the same cents; the method enum → the `invoicesPage.method.*` phrase). `notify.invoice.claimedVia` no longer carries its own preposition ("pagó {method}" / "paid {method}"), so the phrase supplies it once.
**Evidence (2026-11-11, branch fix/ticker-payment off develop 53f3cfc):** RED first — unit `deno test …/notify-on-event/test.ts` → "FAILED | 1 passed | 5 failed" ("Tu cliente pagó 45000" for "$450", "pagó por zelle" for "por Zelle"); int → "FAILED | 7 passed | 1 failed" ("María Pérez pagó" — the amount dropped); e2e `deno test …/notification-controller/e2e.test.ts --filter REQ-224` → "invoice_paid: Tu cliente pagó 45000 / invoice_claimed: María Pérez dice que pagó por zelle — …", the demo's exact lines. GREEN — unit "ok | 6 passed | 0 failed", int "ok | 8 passed | 0 failed", e2e "ok | 8 passed | 0 failed"; neighbours `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/communication src/paperwork/domain/coordinators src/paperwork/entrypoints/{public,revisions,invoice}-controller` → 243 passed, 1 failed (the `smk` real-Postmark smoke test, which needs ../.env and is outside the gate); jest unit "98 passed · 895 passed, 1 skipped"; `deno lint` clean on the touched backend dirs.
## REQ-223 — The topbar's EN/ES toggle is styled, and clear of the search box, on every page that renders it (/assistant included)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11, on the 20-agent demo's findings: "fix every issue the demo found." Demo issues `i18n-formatting-m6` ("EN/ES buttons overlap the search box at 390px (/assistant)") and `i18n-formatting-m11` ("EN/ES toggle unstyled on /assistant (plain boxes), on both screens"); root cause RC-C in `demo-rca.md`.
**Cause (RCA, confirmed by a skeptic pass):** the DashTopbar island (greeting, GlobalSearch, ticker, EN/ES toggle) renders on every app page, but the toggle's rules (`.topbar__lang*`) and the phone rule that hides `.topbar__search` and `.topbar__ticker` at ≤640px lived only in `front-end/static/dashboard.css`. The /assistant routes link only `assistant-page.css`, which has neither, so the toggle drew as two grey browser-default buttons and, at 390px, the search box stayed visible and squeezed the toggle into a column on top of it. Introduced in `a9563b1` (toggle CSS for the dashboard only) and REQ-207 (search in every topbar).
**Requirement:** the toggle's styles and the phone bar's hide rule ship with the DashTopbar island itself (`front-end/lib/topbar-css.ts`, rendered in a `<style>` inside the island, as GlobalSearch does), so every route that renders the bar gets them whatever stylesheet it links; `dashboard.css` no longer carries its own copy. At ≤640px the search box and the ticker are hidden on /assistant as on the dashboard; EN and ES sit on one row, never on the search.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/topbar-chrome.test.ts` ("REQ-223 …": `TOPBAR_CSS` styles the toggle and hides search + ticker ≤640px; DashTopbar renders it; no route stylesheet re-declares `.topbar__lang`; the /assistant routes render DashTopbar without dashboard.css) · integration n/a — pure CSS shipped by an island; no server contract changes, and the browser story measures the rendered result · e2e `e2e/topbar-chrome/topbar-chrome.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-223: …" /assistant and /dashboard at 1440 and 390px: the off button has no border and a transparent background, the lit one is white, EN and ES on one row, the search hidden on a phone and never overlapped).
**Evidence (2026-11-11, branch fix/topbar-css off develop `53f3cfc`):** RED first — jest unit → "Cannot find module '../../front-end/lib/topbar-css'"; the story on the unfixed tree → "1440px: the off button has no border — expected \"none\", got \"outset\"" (m11) and, with the style checks skipped, "/assistant 390px: EN and ES sit on one row (8,33) — expected 33, got 8" (m6: the buttons stacked). ## REQ-231 — Every page renders in the signed-in user's language from the server, so it never flashes Spanish before hydrating
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11, on the 20-agent demo report: "fix every issue the demo found." Demo issues `stage-content-m2` ("Stage shows Spanish for a moment after loading" — pair 8: ~20 s of Spanish island text, ES pressed, English footer, no account card, "Cargando…") and `quote-invoice-money-m11` ("Pair 5: Spanish composer placeholder ('Ej: El cliente quiere una losa…') shown in the English UI"). RCA: `demo-rca.md` (group ssr-lang-flash).
**Cause (reproduced on develop `53f3cfc`):** `langSignal` (front-end/lib/lang.ts) is one module-level signal defaulting to Spanish; on the server nothing set it per request, so every island that reads `t()` / `langSignal.value` was server-rendered Spanish for an English user — while route-level copy given an explicit `lang` (SiteFooter, `<html lang>`) was English. Until the islands hydrated (on the demo stage's replica frame, ~20 s) the page read Spanish: `curl` of `/assistant` for a `language: "en"` account carried `placeholder="Ej: El cliente quiere una losa de 10'x10', ¿cuánto debo cobrar?"`, and `/customers` carried `topbar__lang-btn--on` on ES.
**Requirement:** The server renders every island in the request's language — the page's own (`ctx.state.lang`, REQ-122), else `?lang=`, else the signed-in user's `language`, else the `pm_lang` cookie, else the Spanish-first default — per request, so concurrent requests never share one (an AsyncLocalStorage the root middleware opens; `langSignal.value` reads it on the server only — `front-end/lib/ssr-lang.ts`). The user's own language beats a `pm_lang` cookie another window on the origin left (the staff's pages around a demo's replica frame). `<html lang>` says the same language. The app shell hands it to the browser (`window.__PM_LANG`), and the browser's module-load seed starts from it before `?lang=`/localStorage, so hydration matches the server markup; only a real choice (`?lang=`, the stored one) is ever persisted, never the server's language or the default.
**Not in this change:** why pair 8's frame took ~20 s to hydrate (no trace was captured), and the replica frame and the staff's window sharing one `pm:lang` localStorage (the frame now SSRs and hydrates in the customer's language regardless).
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/ssr-lang.test.ts` (deno: the resolution order; an island SSR'd for an English user renders the English composer placeholder, a Spanish user's Spanish; two interleaved requests each render their own language; the default outside a request; `bootLangScript`; `pickClientLang` takes the server's language first and persists only a real choice), `jest/unit/ssr-lang-flash.test.ts` (the wiring, in the gate: the middleware ahead of `fsRoutes()`, the shell's `resolveSsrLang`/`bootLangScript`, the seed reading `__PM_LANG`, `node:async_hooks` only in the server module) · integration `jest/integration/ssr-lang-flash.int.test.ts` (over the dev stack: an English account's `/assistant` server HTML carries the English placeholder and `window.__PM_LANG="en"`, also with a `pm_lang=es` cookie; `/customers` has EN pressed; a Spanish account still gets Spanish) · e2e `e2e/ssr-lang-flash/ssr-lang-flash.e2e.test.ts` (a browser held on the server markup — no script file loads: the composer placeholder is English, EN pressed, `<html lang="en">`; hydrated, the placeholder is still English).
**Evidence (2026-11-11, branch fix/ssr-lang-flash off develop `53f3cfc`, stack on :22009):** RED first — deno unit: "TS2307 Cannot find module … lib/ssr-lang.ts" / "no exported member 'pickClientLang'"; jest unit: 4 failed (ENOENT `lib/ssr-lang.ts`, no `ssrLangMiddleware` in main.ts); jest int: 4 failed (`Expected substring: "placeholder=\"Ex: Customer wants a 10'x10' slab, what should I charge?\""` — the HTML was `<html lang="es">` with the Spanish placeholder); e2e: `expected "Ex: Customer wants a 10'x10' slab, what should I charge?", got "Ej: El cliente quiere una losa de 10'x10', ¿cuánto debo cobrar?"` and `EN is the pressed language (EN class: "topbar__lang-btn ")`. GREEN — `deno test -A lib/ssr-lang.test.ts lib/dash-cache.test.ts` → "ok | 17 passed | 0 failed"; `npx jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 99 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 899 passed"; `npx jest integration/ssr-lang-flash integration/assistant-from-prop integration/landing-pages integration/contract-lang` → "Tests: 17 passed"; `shots run e2e/ssr-lang-flash e2e/contract-lang e2e/assistant-shell e2e/legal-pages` → "14 pass · 0 fail". `deno check` (whole front-end) shows the same 8 errors develop has (Timeout/number in DemoModeOverlay, DemoStage, Landing2*, transport; AsstChat `find`), none new; `deno lint` clean on every touched file.
## REQ-230 — The assistant's in-flight flow lives on the conversation: any reload, in any window, rebuilds it (demo issue M14)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11, on the 20-agent demo report: "fix every issue the demo found." Demo issue **M14** — "Reloading the stage can't recover the assistant flow; server holds only the first user message" (RCA in `demo-rca.md`, verdict CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD).
**Cause (RCA, re-checked at develop `53f3cfc`):** the P-22 early mint (`176f66f`) put the conversation's id in the address bar but saved only the typed note (`POST /agents/conversations/:id/draft {note}` → one user message). The job options, the pick, the price, `pickerMode`, `priceCaptureOpen`, `previewCtaId` and the rest were island `useState` plus a per-tab sessionStorage back-stack (`AsstChat.tsx` ViewSnapshot / `persistStackAs`); the first real server writes came only at price Continue. So before Continue `GET /agents/conversations/:id` held one user message, and any reload — the contractor's own, or the demo stage, which is an independent copy of the app with no access to the contractor's sessionStorage — painted that one bubble and nothing else.
**Requirement:** The assistant's in-flight flow — the chip that opened it, the typed details, the job options as edited, the selected and the confirmed option, the price step and its value, the suggested tiers, the open picker, the open quote review, the raw details that still owe the end-of-wizard picker — is stored ON the conversation, server-side, as one typed object (`shared/quote-flow/assistant-draft.ts`): the island writes it (debounced) on every change via `POST /agents/conversations/:id/draft { draft }` (`null` clears it; anything not a draft object is ignored; every field type-checked and bounded; owner only; its own KV key, removed with the conversation), and `GET /agents/conversations/:id` returns it as `draft`. The thread route hands it to the island, which seeds its state from it at SSR, so a reload in any window lands on the same step with the same values. Before Continue every panel comes back as it was; after Continue (a quote is bound) the pre-quote panels stay closed while their data (the pick, the price) is kept, the end-of-wizard picker and an open review come back (the review only if its CTA is still in the transcript). A load that lands mid-request re-asks for the options / price tiers. A plain chat never writes a draft. Not in scope (others own it): the stage's DOM mirror and its reload trigger (B1/M12).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/assistant-draft.test.ts` ("REQ-230 (M14) …": the wire shape round-trips; non-objects refused; malformed fields dropped; bounds; blank draft; what a reload paints before/after Continue; restored bullet ids never collide; the route passes `initialDraft`, the island seeds its state from it and writes `{draft}`) · integration `backend/src/agents/entrypoints/conversations-controller/e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-230 (M14) …" on the booted app: `{draft}` saved and returned to another session's GET; replace / `null` clears / garbage ignored; binding the quote keeps it; a stranger is refused; DELETE removes it) · e2e `e2e/assistant-draft/assistant-draft.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-230 (M14) …": details typed → price typed, no Continue → the server holds the step; another browser context opens the thread and SSR-paints the price step with the details and the price; the contractor's own reload too).
**Evidence (2026-11-11, branch fix/m14 off develop `53f3cfc`):** RED first — jest unit → "Test Suites: 1 failed" (Cannot find module `shared/quote-flow/assistant-draft`); the controller test → TS2339 "Property 'getDraft' does not exist on type 'AgentConversationStore'", and with `--no-check` the four REQ-230 cases FAILED (`draft` undefined); the e2e on a stack at `PORT=5747` → "✗ … expectation failed: the server knows the price step is open — expected true, got undefined". GREEN — jest unit `--testPathPattern assistant-draft` → "Tests: 14 passed"; full jest unit → "Test Suites: 99 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 909 passed"; `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --parallel src/agents` → "ok | 209 passed | 0 failed"; `shots run e2e/assistant-draft e2e/assistant-shell e2e/assistant-threads-scroll` twice → "5 pass · 0 fail" both times. `deno lint` clean on every touched file; `deno check` on the island shows only the two TS errors develop already has (`ClientsPageResponse.find`, AsstChat.tsx ~3617 — identical with this change stashed).
## REQ-222 — Demo issue M11: after a demo ends, the customer's app keeps asking for one, so a new demo reaches it without a reload

**Requirement (Raphael, 2026-11-11):** "fix every issue the demo found" — this entry is the 20-agent demo's M11: "After a demo ends, the customer's app stops polling /active, so a new demo never reaches them until they reload." After a CONNECTED demo ends — from the staff side or from the customer's own End — the customer's app goes back to asking `GET /demo-mode/active` every 5 s (REQ-153 AMENDMENT "same screen at once": "every 5 s while not connected"), so a new demo joins on its own within the poll, the page never reloaded.
**Root cause (RCA `demo-rca.md` M11, skeptic UPHELD):** `DemoModeOverlay.tsx`'s poll was a self-scheduling `setTimeout` chain that re-armed only while `!peerOnlineRef.current`; connected, the chain stopped by design, and only a visibility change or `onStatus` on a drop that was NOT `ended` restarted it. `onEnded`, the customer's `end()` and the link cleanup cleared the demo but never asked again, so the chain stayed dead for the life of the page (introduced in d226b76). Fix: the poll is `front-end/lib/demo-mode/active-poll.ts` (`now()` / `idle()` / `stop()`, one timer at most, an ask in flight re-arms on answer), and the overlay re-arms it from the connection STATE — an effect on `[peerOnline, demo?.id]` calls `idle()` whenever this side is not connected, the end included.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-mode-active-poll.test.ts` ("REQ-222 …": asks at once then every 5 s; stops while connected; the demo ends from the connected state → an ask within 5 s and a new demo picked up; an ask in flight when the link drops re-arms; a failed ask keeps polling; no doubled chain; stopped asks nothing; the overlay drives its poll with `activePoll` and re-arms on `!peerOnline`) · integration n/a — no backend change; `GET /demo-mode/active` is REQ-153's, covered by its controller int test · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-restart.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-222 (M11): …": a connected demo ended by staff, then one ended by the customer, and each time the next demo connects on the customer's never-reloaded page).
**Evidence (2026-11-11, local, worktree `fix/m11` off origin/develop `53f3cfc`):** RED — jest with the old chain extracted verbatim into `active-poll.ts` → "Tests: 2 failed, 6 passed" ("the demo ends from the connected state …: Expected: 3 Received: 2"; the overlay not using `activePoll`); `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-restart.e2e.test.ts` against the old overlay (`PORT=57391 deno task serve`) → "✗ REQ-222 (M11) … · the demo after a staff End: the customer's app never connected". GREEN — jest unit "Test Suites: 99 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 903 passed, 904 total"; `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-restart.e2e.test.ts` → "✓ REQ-222 (M11) … · 18.1s"; neighbours `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-mode.e2e.test.ts e2e/demo-mode/demo-presenters.e2e.test.ts` → "✓ REQ-153 + … · 14s", "✓ REQ-214 … · 5.3s"; fmt/lint/`deno check` clean on the touched files.
## REQ-235 — Demo mode: the end of a demo is said on both sides and stays; End asks first
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11, on the 20-agent demo's findings ("Per issue. … Read the issue. Read the root cause analysis. Write a test. And then make it green.") — issue `demo-lifecycle-m2`, "No lasting 'demo ended' message on either side, and End has no confirmation" (pairs 3, 4, 6, 8, 10: "Pill + your pointer just vanished … No 'demo ended' message/toast at all"; fleet-9: "no message saying who ended it"); root cause in `demo-rca.md` (CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD).
**Cause:** "The demo ended" existed only as the pill's status chip, for 0.8–1.5 s: the customer's overlay dropped the demo 1.5 s after `ended` (800 ms after its own End); a stage showed the chip as long, then went to a bare /admin with nothing said there. `ended` said which side ended it (`by`), never which presenter (REQ-214). Both End buttons ended the demo for everyone on one click (`onClick={end}`).
**Requirement:** Who ended it is said, on both sides, and it stays. An `ended` a presenter caused carries their `pid` — a stage's End over the socket or over HTTP, and a presenter's Demo on another customer that leaves the old demo with nobody on it; the customer's never carries one. The customer's pill turns at once, in place, into a notice that stays until dismissed (×) or a new demo starts: "{name} ended the demo" (the presenter, by name), "You ended the demo" (their own End, from any tab), "The demo ended" when nobody can be named. A stage still hands its presenter their own account back on /admin (REQ-153 AMENDMENT), now carrying who ended it (`/admin?demo=ended&by=you|other&name=…`); /admin shows the same lasting notice — "You ended the demo" (this presenter, any of their windows), "{customer} ended the demo", "{colleague} ended the demo" — and drops the parameters from the address at once, so a reload does not say it again. They are read on /admin only, as text, a name of at most 80 characters. End asks first, in place, without a modal: the first click turns End into "End for everyone?" with "Yes, end it" and "Keep going"; Keep going, or 4 s without an answer, puts End back and nothing has ended. "Yes, end it" ends the demo for everyone (REQ-214) and shows it at once, before the server answers (REQ-179): the customer's notice, the stage's "The demo ended". It is disabled for its first 400 ms, so the second click of a double click on End never ends a demo.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-mode-ended.test.ts` ("REQ-235 …": `ended` parses with a presenter's `pid` and never a viewer's; `whoEnded` on the customer's side and on a stage; the line each says; `endedHref` / `readEndedNotice` round trips, other parameters kept, junk and over-long names; `endConfirm` — the question, the arm, Yes once, Keep going, the 4 s; both dictionaries; the transport, the shared `EndDemo` component and both islands wired), `backend/src/demo-mode/domain/coordinators/demo-hub/test.ts` ("REQ-235 an end by a presenter names them …"); the REQ-153 / REQ-187 wiring checks in `jest/unit/demo-mode-protocol.test.ts` and `jest/unit/demo-mode-replica.test.ts` now find End in `EndDemo` and the stage's hop in `endedHref` · integration `backend/src/demo-mode/entrypoints/demo-mode-controller/int.test.ts` ("REQ-235 …": a colleague's HTTP End, a presenter's socket End and a presenter's Demo on another customer each reach the sockets as `ended` with that presenter's `pid`; the customer's HTTP End carries none); the REQ-214 case's End now expects Hans's `pid` · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-ended.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-235: …": End asks, Keep going and the 4 s put it back with the demo still on; the customer's End says "You ended the demo" at once on her screen — before the server answers — and "Ana Torres ended the demo" on /admin, the address bare, both still there seconds later; the staff's End says "The demo ended" at once on the stage, "You ended the demo" on /admin, "Hans ended the demo" on hers until she dismisses it); the REQ-153 and REQ-214 stories end through the two steps.
**Evidence (2026-11-11, worktree fix/demo-m2 off origin/develop 53f3cfc):** RED first, each for its own reason — jest `Test Suites: 3 failed` (`Could not locate module ../../shared/demo-mode/ended.ts`; ENOENT `components/demo-mode/EndDemo.tsx`; `Expected pattern: /location\.href = endedHref\(/`); `demo-hub/test.ts` and the controller int test → type-check failed (`'pid' does not exist in type '{ t: "ended"; by: Role; reason?: … }'`, `hub.end` "Expected 2-3 arguments, but got 4"); `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-ended.e2e.test.ts` → `✗ … locator.waitFor: Timeout 2000ms exceeded` waiting for `demo-end-ask` (the first click on End ended the demo). GREEN — jest unit project `99 passed, 909 passed, 1 skipped`; `deno test src/demo-mode` → `ok | 18 passed | 0 failed` (hub 4/4, controller int 6/6); `shots run e2e/demo-mode` → `3 pass · 0 fail` (REQ-153 14.8 s, REQ-214 6.1 s, REQ-235 23.8 s; the frames show the stage's "End for everyone?", "The demo ended" on the stage, "Ana Torres ended the demo" on /admin, "Hans ended the demo" on the customer's phone). `deno check` + `deno lint` on every touched file clean; the whole front-end's `deno lint` (22 problems: `static/meta-pixel-fake.js`, `InvoicesPage.tsx`) and `deno check` (8 errors: `Timeout` vs `number`, `ClientsPageResponse.find`) are the same on a clean checkout of 53f3cfc, none in this change; `deno fmt --check` clean on every touched TS/JSON file; en/es each 3564 keys, no key in one only.
## REQ-228 — The demo pills never cover the page: the customer's pill stays clear of every control, and the stage's pill stays off the frame
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11: "fix every issue the demo found". The stage kept a fixed `INSET.bottom = 76` under the frame for a pill that wraps on a narrow window and then rises over the frame (`DemoStage.tsx`).

It tries the four corners first (bottom-left leads), then the left and right edges from the bottom up. It stays put while its spot is clear and moves when the page under it changes (re-checked every 0.7 s, after a scroll or resize, and when the pill changes size). When no spot is clear, it takes the spot with the fewest controls under it. At 640 px wide or less it is compact: the first presenter's colour dot, the status and End. Tapping the status shows the details (title, "… is guiding you", the presenters), and that text is its label and tooltip. On the staff stage, the band under the frame is the pill's measured height plus its 14 px offset plus a 10 px gap (`ResizeObserver`), not a guessed 76 px. ## REQ-221 — No duplicate polling: the demo replica frame and hidden tabs do not poll conversations, notifications or the quote preview
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11, on the 20-agent demo report: "fix every issue the demo found". Demo issue `pointer-and-replica-side-effects-polling` ("Heavy polling of /api/agents/conversations?limit=50 and /api/notifications?limit=10"), RCA in `demo-rca.md` (verdict LIKELY, skeptic UPHELD; related M6, pair 4).
**Cause (RCA, re-checked on develop `53f3cfc`):** every island ran its own bare `setInterval` in every document — `AsstThreads` conversations(50) every 8 s plus on mount and on each tab show, `DashTopbar` notifications(10) every 10 s and unread-count every 30 s, `AsstChat`'s quote preview every 8 s. None checked `isReplicaFrame()` and none paused while the tab was hidden, so the demo stage's replica frame (REQ-187, a full live copy of the customer's app, reloaded on each of their navigations) doubled every poll, and a backgrounded tab kept them all going. The 1–2 s rate the agents quoted is not in the code (it came from untimed request indices); the duplication is.
**Requirement:** every app poll goes through one scheduler, `front-end/lib/poll.ts` `startPoll(fn, ms, { immediate })`, which: never runs inside the demo stage's replica frame (no timer, no call); does not tick while the document is hidden and catches up once when it is shown; never starts a tick while the previous one is in flight; swallows a failed fetch. `AsstThreads`, `DashTopbar` (both polls; P-67's stop on `pm:logout`/`pagehide` kept) and `AsstChat`'s quote-preview poll use it.
**Not done here (RCA's longer-term option):** one SSE/WebSocket channel per user replacing the timers.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/polling.test.ts` ("REQ-221 …": the scheduler's period, immediate call, replica no-op, hidden pause + catch-up, starts-hidden, no stacking, swallowed errors; the three islands make their polled calls through `startPoll`, not `setInterval`) · integration n/a — no server change; the behaviour is the browser's request schedule, covered by the e2e · e2e `e2e/polling/polling.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-221: …" in a browser on /assistant: the visible page polls both endpoints; the same page as `<iframe name="pm-demo-replica">` sends neither in 11.5 s; a hidden page sends neither and catches up when shown).
**Evidence (2026-11-11, local, branch fix/pointer-polling off develop `53f3cfc`):** RED first — jest unit → "Cannot find module '../../front-end/lib/poll'"; with the scheduler alone, "Tests: 5 failed, 8 passed" (the islands' wiring); `shots run e2e/polling` against `PORT=48693 deno task serve` → "expectation failed: the replica frame fetched no conversations — expected 0, got 2" (the visible-page control passed). GREEN — jest `polling` 13/13; full jest unit "Test Suites: 99 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 908 passed"; `shots run e2e/polling` → "✓ REQ-221 … 45.3s". `deno lint` clean on the four touched front-end files; `deno check` clean on `lib/poll.ts`, `AsstThreads.tsx`, `DashTopbar.tsx` (`AsstChat.tsx` carries two pre-existing TS errors at the `cs.find` line, identical on develop); `deno fmt --check` clean on every touched file but `AsstChat.tsx` (known-unformattable).
## REQ-233 — One agreement, one bill: a quote-linked invoice never bills past what is still unbilled (demo B2)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11: "fix every issue the demo found" — demo issue **B2** ("One $2,400 job billed $4,800: signing makes deposit+balance invoices, then 'Send as Invoice' makes a third, full-amount invoice"), root cause in `demo-rca.md` (B2, CONFIRMED + skeptic UPHELD).
**Requirement:** Signing a quote bills it (deposit + balance). After that, nothing can bill the same agreement a second time by accident: `POST /invoices` with a `quoteId` refuses an amount past the quote's remaining-to-invoice (quote total + approved change orders − every non-void invoice on it; tax is not part of the agreed price) with 409 `exceeds_agreement` (`agreementTotalCents`, `invoicedCents`, `remainingCents`, `requestedCents`). Extra work billed on purpose says `override: true` (a flag, never stored). A REQ-200 retry of a create that already landed still gets its invoice back. In the assistant, an accepted quote offers no Quote ⇄ Invoice swap (the Invoice pill and Send are disabled), and the swap bills only the ledger's unbilled remainder — never the full total — and refuses with "This agreement is already invoiced in full…" when nothing is left. The invoice form and the assistant show the 409 as a sentence (en + es), not "POST /invoices failed: 409".
**Out of scope here:** the review card re-opening after a reload (in-memory `reviewedCtas`, demo m5) — a separate issue; with this guard it can no longer over-bill.

## REQ-236 — A failed send is not a sent quote, anywhere (demo M8)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11, on the 20-agent demo report: "fix every issue the demo found" — this entry is demo issue **M8** ("A failed send still shows as sent everywhere (header, list, /quotes, open story); the failure card has a check-box icon; the old failure card stays after a good resend"). Root cause: `demo-rca.md` § M8 (analyst + skeptic, UPHELD).
**Cause (RCA, re-checked at develop `53f3cfc`):** being "sent" was not tied to being delivered. `SendQuote` stamped `sentAt`/status `sent` and emitted `quote:sent` BEFORE dispatch and set `conv.quoteStatus = "sent"` whatever happened; no delivery outcome was stored on the quote. So `BuildQuoteCards.deriveStage` (status/sentAt/opens only) said "Just sent" / "Out for response"; `readingFor` gave every 0-open quote the email/spam story; the chat set `quote.status = "sent"` on any HTTP 200 so the header read "Out for signature"; the failure divider and card drew `ICN.contract` (a tick in a box); and the recovery-form scan skipped past a newer SUCCESS divider to re-attach the form to an older failure.
**Requirement:** A send that reaches nobody leaves the quote unsent, and every surface says so: (1) `SendQuote` stores each attempt's outcome on the quote (`lastDelivery` = when, channel, where it went or why not) and only when a channel delivered stamps `deliveredAt`/`sentAt`, flips a draft to `sent` and emits `quote:sent`; the conversation's `quoteStatus` is `undelivered` until a send reaches the customer. (2) A quote whose last send reached nobody and that was never delivered has the `/quotes` stage `undelivered` ("Not delivered", amber, in the drafts track, CTA "Fix contact + resend", story "Not delivered… fix their email or phone"), is not counted as awaiting in the pipeline, and is never "Just sent" / "Out for response" — whatever status LockQuote left on it. Acceptance still wins. (3) A texted quote with no opens gets no email/spam wording. (4) The chat header reads "Not delivered · fix contact" after a failed send (never "Out for signature" / "Quote sent"); the local quote flips to `sent` only when the divider names a delivery. (5) The failure divider and the failed send card draw a warning triangle, not a tick. (6) The contact-recovery form rides only the NEWEST send divider — a good resend retires the older failure. (7) The thread list chip reads "Not delivered".
**Not changed (other issues' scope):** LockQuote still flips status to `sent` and stamps `sentAt` at lock (demo M3) — this entry reads the stored delivery outcome over that status, it does not change lock.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/failed-send-truth.test.ts` ("REQ-236 …": `isUndelivered`/`deliveryFromDivider`; the pipeline classifier; `sendDividerFailed`, `headerStatusKey`, `applySendOutcome`, `lastRecoveryDividerId` (newer success retires the old failure); `OUT_STAGES`/`DRAFT_TRACK_STAGES`, label/mood/CTA/story for `undelivered`, no spam/email copy for an SMS quote; wiring: `ICN.alert` on the failure divider and card, the chat uses the helpers, the thread chip, both languages) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/send-quote/int.test.ts` ("REQ-236 …": failed send leaves the quote draft with no sentAt and no `quote:sent`, stores the failure, conv `undelivered`; a LockQuote-sent quote still reads undelivered; a good resend after a failure sends it, `quote:sent` once; a success records where it went), `backend/src/analytics/domain/coordinators/build-quote-cards/int.test.ts` ("REQ-236 …": stage `undelivered` for a status-sent and for a draft quote whose send failed; a once-delivered quote stays `sent` after a failed resend; acceptance beats it) · e2e `backend/src/agents/entrypoints/conversations-controller/failed-send.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-236 e2e …", the booted app over HTTP: send-quote by SMS to a customer with no phone → `GET /quotes` stage `undelivered`, `GET /quotes/:id` `lastDelivery` failure and no `deliveredAt`, `GET /agents/conversations` `quoteStatus` `undelivered`; add an email, resend → stage `sent`, `quoteStatus` `sent`, `deliveredAt`). Browser (shots) story: n/a here — driving a real failed send in a browser needs the whole wizard; the client-side readings are pinned by the jest unit file and the server truth by the booted-app e2e.
**Evidence (2026-11-11, branch fix/m8 off develop `53f3cfc`):** RED first — backend `deno test --no-check` on the two int files → `FAILED | 25 passed | 6 failed` ("a failed send is not a sent quote": Actual `sent` / Expected `draft`; stage Actual `sent` / Expected `undelivered`; `deliveredAt stamped`); with type-check → TS2339 `lastDelivery`/`deliveredAt` do not exist on `Quote`; jest → "Cannot find module ../../shared/quote-flow/delivery.ts"; the e2e against the pre-fix code → `quoteStatus` Actual `sent` / Expected `undelivered`. GREEN — `deno test -A --unstable-kv` over send-quote, lock-quote, conversations-controller (incl. the new e2e), build-quote-cards, compute-dashboard-stats, list-active-jobs, compute-quote-win-rate, quotes-controller, dashboard-controller, quote-store, send-paperwork-email/-sms → `ok | 106 passed | 0 failed`; `jest --selectProjects unit --ci` → `Test Suites: 99 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 910 passed`; `deno check` on the touched islands/libs → only the two errors develop already has (AsstChat `ClientsPageResponse.find`, present at `53f3cfc`); `deno check backend/bootstrap/mod.ts` clean; `deno lint` clean on every touched front-end, backend and shared file; `deno fmt` clean on every touched file that was clean before (AsstChat.tsx was not).

## REQ-267 — A chat correction that re-drafts the quote always gets a text reply saying what changed
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11, on the 20-agent demo: "fix every issue the demo found". Demo issue `ai-assistant-p1-noreply` (Pair 1: "My correction fixed the paint line, but the assistant gave no text reply"; deposit silently ignored — related M22). **Cause:** a correction goes to the LLM, which calls `create_quote` again and often returns no prose; `OpenAILLMClient.respond` maps that to `""` (`fallbackTextFor`), and `HandleChatMessage` suppressed the text bubble for every card-bearing action with empty (or customer-ask-only) text (#36, meant for the first draft's "Drafting a quote." filler). The updated draft landed as a bare card, and anything `create_quote` cannot carry (a deposit) vanished without a word.
**Requirement:** when `create_quote` revises the conversation's bound draft and the model gave no usable prose, the coordinator writes the reply itself from the old → new line items: lines removed, added (with amount), repriced, and the total when it moved; if the contractor asked for a deposit (EN/ES wording), the reply says the deposit is chosen in the payment step after lock-in. In the contractor's language. The first draft keeps the #36 suppression (card only).

## REQ-266 — Job options keep every scope item the contractor named, in the contractor's own trade words
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-11 ("fix every issue the demo found") — demo issue `ai-assistant-p7-options` ("Pair 7: job options drop details and bullet 1 was silently reworded"); RCA in `demo-rca.md` (verdict CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD).
**Requirement:** A long, specific job description (the demo's 900-character bathroom gut: demo, curbless shower, slab cut, glass, 72" vanity, hex mosaic, two faucets, fan, lights, permit) produces job options that keep every one of those items — none is cut to keep an option at four lines. The contractor's trade words survive the cleanup ("Gutted old fixtures and tile" is not reworded to "Removed …"). Root cause: the options prompt demanded "3 or 4 bullets — no more, no fewer" and the anti-echo rule (REQ-026) said "rewrite every bullet", and three code paths then cut each option with a hard `.slice(0, 4)` — the backend normalizer of the model's reply, its heuristic fallback, and the island's last-resort fallback (`AsstChat.tsx` `localFallbackOptions`); the "wider scope" variant even kept only 3 items + cleanup. Now: one shared rule `shared/quote-flow/option-bullets.ts` (`MAX_OPTION_BULLETS = 12`, `widerBullets` = every bullet + jobsite cleanup once) is used by all three paths; the prompt (en and es dictionaries, identical) asks for 3–12 bullets, requires every distinct scope item as its own bullet in at least the detailed option, and keeps the anti-echo rule while keeping the contractor's own trade verbs and terms.
**Not done here:** a visible "reworded" marker on bullets that differ from the contractor's words (the RCA's optional UI idea) — the root cause was the prompt forcing the paraphrase, fixed above.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/option-bullets.test.ts` ("REQ-266 …": the cap holds a ten-item job; the wider version is every item + cleanup; the island fallback and the backend coordinator use the shared rule, no `.slice(0, 4)`) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/generate-job-options/int.test.ts` ("REQ-266 ai-assistant-p7-options …": a ten-bullet model reply survives whole; the honest fallback keeps ten typed lines; the prompt has no 3–4 cap, asks for every scope item, keeps "gutted"; the fallback wider version is never shorter than the full one) · e2e n/a — the bullet count and wording are decided in the backend coordinator and its prompt, covered against a fake LLM at integration level; a browser run would only replay that fake reply through the picker, which already renders any number of bullets.
